species: Babesia sp. with Ehrlichia canis (mixed, unspecified)
rationale: Crossref metadata show it was published online on 2006-10-17 (print 2006-11-15, Comp Clin Pathol 15(4)). That is before the window opens on 2006-10-23. No abstract was available.
PubMed (PMID 16522352) gives the e-publication date as 2006-03-07, before the window. Going by the abstract, it is otherwise a clinical, diagnostic and molecular review of B. conradae.
Crossref and the landing-page metadata date it to In Practice 28(7), July 2006, before the window. The summary describes a general practice review of epidemiology, signs, diagnosis and treatment.
PubMed (PMID 17020140) dates it to Acta Vet Hung 54(3), September 2006, before the window. Its content would otherwise be eligible: the abstract reports complications, MODS, SIRS and DIC in 63 dogs.

species: B. gibsoni (stated in title, method unknown)
rationale: Title only, and it could not be found in PubMed. The title suggests a case report of a distinct renal syndrome (protein-losing nephropathy), which would be eligible. The PubMed record found (Slade 2011, JAAHA) is a different paper.
Title only, and the title is cut off ('Canine babesiosis in'). Neither eligibility nor content can be judged, so it goes to full-text review.

species: B. canis (stated in title, method unknown)
rationale: Title only, and it could not be found in PubMed. The title suggests a case report of a distinct renal syndrome (nephrotic syndrome) linked to B. canis, which would be eligible.

species: B. rossi (experimental challenge; heterologous B. canis antigens)
rationale: Experimental challenge in vaccinated and control dogs reporting host immune protection, clinical signs, parasitaemia and development of anaemia. It reports host responses to infection, not only vaccine efficacy.

PubMed (PMID 16815635) gives the e-publication date as 2006-07-03, before the window. The abstract shows it is also an antigen characterisation (Bg12D3) with only an antibody response, so it is parasite antigen work.

PubMed (PMID 16962707) gives the e-publication date as 2006-09-08, before the window. The abstract shows the review is also about species characterisation, tick biology and prevention, not pathophysiology.
Tick transmission of B. divergens in an in vitro skin-feeding model, with no dog data.
Identification of a secreted antigen and its use in ELISA serodiagnosis, with no host pathophysiological data.

species: Babesia sp. with Ehrlichia canis (mixed, unspecified)
rationale: No abstract in PubMed or Europe PMC, and the Springer page could not be reached. This is endocrine data (cortisol, insulin, T3/T4) in chronic ehrlichiosis with or without babesiosis (Vet Res Commun 30(8), Nov 2006). Whether a co-infected subgroup gives separable Babesia-related host data can only be judged from the full text.

species: B. gibsoni with Ehrlichia canis (mixed, unspecified)
rationale: No abstract in PubMed or Europe PMC, and the Springer page could not be reached. The title and MeSH terms show a comparison of oxidative stress, lipid peroxidation and haematocrit between E. canis mono-infected and E. canis plus B. gibsoni co-infected dogs. Whether the Babesia contribution can be separated needs the full text.
Molecular prevalence survey of haemoprotozoa in dogs and foxes, with no host pathophysiological data.
Acute phase proteins (CRP, SAA, haptoglobin), ESR, WBC, HCT and platelets in naturally infected dogs against healthy controls, with follow-up after treatment. Already in the review as BG004.
Development of a PCR-RFLP assay, with no host data.
Cloning of a RAP-1 antigen and its use as an ELISA diagnostic antigen, with no host pathophysiology.
PubMed (PMID 16777097) gives the e-publication date as 2006-06-14, before the window. The abstract shows it is also antigen characterisation (BgAMA-1) with antibody kinetics only.
Ticks from passerine birds and their pathogens, with no dog Babesia data.

From the abstract: the study measures ELISA sensitivity and false-negative rates. 'Anaemic dogs' is only a label for one group, and no haematological or other host pathophysiological data are reported, so the rescue does not hold.
rescue_reason: Borderline rescue. Diagnostic ELISA study that characterises the infected dogs by acute infection and by anaemia (a host clinical feature), so host data may be present even though no haematology values are reported; the adjudicator should check the full text.

rationale: Seroprevalence survey of tick-borne agents in Ontario and Quebec, with no host pathophysiological data.

species: Babesia sp. (confirmed, real-time PCR; mostly imported)
rationale: From the abstract: a 7-case series of severely ill dogs, with clinical, laboratory and outcome data for each case. The aim is diagnostic, but the full text may hold a clinicopathological profile of severe cases, which counts as an eligible case series.
rescue_reason: Borderline rescue. Seven dogs with laboratory data and severe clinical signs were all PCR-positive, while most were smear-negative and seronegative; this dissociation of severity from parasitaemia may be a host-response observation, so the routine-case exclusion looks questionable.

species: Babesia rossi (South Africa; severely anaemic babesiosis)
rationale: Compares serum urea, creatinine and cystatin-C in severely anaemic infected dogs and controls, and concludes the raised urea:creatinine ratio is not of renal origin. This is a mechanistic renal function study.

species: Large Babesia (B. canis, natural infection; species not confirmed by PCR)
rationale: Haematological profile of 248 naturally infected dogs (anaemia indices, thrombocytopenia, leucogram, erythrocyte morphology). This is a clinicopathological profile of infected dogs.

species: B. gibsoni antigen in B. microti-infected mice
rationale: A mouse vaccine model using a B. gibsoni antigen against B. microti, with no dog infection data.
Development of an immunochromatographic test, with no host pathophysiology.
B. bigemina in cattle fever ticks, with no dog data.

Title only, and it could not be found in PubMed. A report of autochthonous canine babesiosis in Germany (2007) may describe clinical and laboratory findings in affected dogs or may be only epidemiological, so it cannot be judged without the full text.

PubMed (PMID 17055131) gives the e-publication date as 2006-10-10, before the window (issue Vaccine 25(7), 2007). The abstract reports IgG2 and IFN-gamma host responses, so it would otherwise have been considered.

Title only. Crossref has no abstract, and the Thieme landing page is behind a bot check. The title shows a homoeopathic treatment report (Trinitrotoluenum 200C), so anaemia is the treatment target rather than a studied mechanism, and the exclusion stands.
rescue_reason: No abstract is available, and the title concerns clinical management of anaemia associated with babesiosis in dogs. Anaemia is a host haematological outcome, so the title does not rule out host data; the adjudicator should read the landing page.

rationale: Prevalence of tick-borne pathogens in domestic animals in Sicily, with no host pathophysiological data.
Climate modelling of Dirofilaria incubation in the UK, with no Babesia data.

species: B. gibsoni Asian genotype (confirmed, PCR and sequencing)
rationale: From the abstract: two routine autochthonous cases with molecular identification. The haematological signs are only called 'consistent with babesiosis', with no values and no distinct syndrome, so the case-report exclusion applies.
rescue_reason: Borderline rescue. Report of the first two autochthonous B. gibsoni (Asian genotype) cases in dogs in Germany, with the abstract stating haematologic signs in both dogs; that reports host haematology, which the stated reason (other_out_of_scope) does not reflect, though the values are not given.

rationale: PCR detection of Hepatozoon in foxes, with no dog Babesia data.
Ticks and tick-borne pathogens collected from animals in the Netherlands, with no host data.

species: Large Babesia (B. canis, natural infection; species not confirmed by PCR)
rationale: Serum biochemistry (liver enzymes, creatinine, urea, albumin, glucose) of 202 infected dogs, interpreted as hepatopathy, renal failure and hypoglycaemia. This is a clinicopathological profile.
PCR monitoring of B. microti in mice, with no dog data.

species: B. canis and other canine Babesia (review)
rationale: From the abstract: a Polish narrative review of human and canine babesiosis whose title includes pathogenesis and which is indexed under host-parasite interactions. The English abstract covers only aetiology and diagnostics, so whether canine pathophysiology is covered needs the full text.
Seasonal prevalence by blood smear in Lahore, with no host pathophysiological data.

species: Babesia sp. (unspecified, smear) with Ehrlichia and Hepatozoon co-infection
rationale: Based on abstract: a single puppy with triple co-infection, so the anaemia, thrombocytopenia and hypergammaglobulinaemia cannot be attributed to Babesia, and no distinct Babesia syndrome or mechanism is described.
rescue_reason: Case of mixed Babesia, Ehrlichia and Hepatozoon infection in a puppy reports persistent anaemia and thrombocytopenia plus hypergammaglobulinaemia. Haematology in an infected dog meets the rescue rule, but Babesia-specific data may not separate from the other pathogens, so the adjudicator should decide.

rationale: Epidemiological description of 495 cases in Cantabria (seasonality, breed, age) with no host pathophysiological data in the abstract.
Retrospective frequency study by breed and age based on blood smears. No host pathophysiology is reported.
Seroprevalence and seasonality survey of dogs in Minas Gerais, with no host pathophysiological data.
Genetic identification and prevalence of a piroplasm in river otters. No dog data.
Comparison of diagnostic assays for equine piroplasmosis. No dog data.
Anti-erythrocyte antibodies in naturally infected cattle. Dogs are mentioned only as background.

species: Babesia sp. (unspecified) with E. canis co-infection
rationale: Based on Springer landing-page abstract: single fatal dog with concurrent babesiosis and ehrlichiosis (anaemia, thrombocytopenia, seizures); the neurological signs are attributed to the co-infection, so Babesia-specific host data cannot be separated.

Case report of abdominal compartment syndrome as a complication of babesiosis, with raised intra-abdominal pressure, respiratory distress and reduced urine output. It describes a distinct complication and reviews its pathophysiology.
Ectoparasite survey of four-striped mice. B. canis is mentioned only as a pathogen those parasites may transmit.

Duplicate record of https://openalex.org/W1486145338 (same four authors, Spanish title of the same Venezuelan isolate study), which reports an experimental infection with PCV, temperature and parasitaemia in dogs; based on title, authors and the abstract of the duplicate.

species: B. gibsoni, B. canis canis, B. vogeli, B. rossi (hsp70 sequences)
rationale: hsp70 gene cloning and phylogeny of canine Babesia isolates, with no host data.
Human case report on TNF blockade and severe babesiosis. No dog data.
Protein C activity in dogs with babesiosis before and after therapy. It reports decreased protein C, anaemia and raised liver enzymes and bilirubin, which are host coagulation and organ-injury data.
Based on Crossref metadata (no abstract; landing page gave no text): a one-page item (p. 184) in a practitioner magazine, a short general note with no original data and not a pathophysiology review.

Based on abstract: a routine single case of diagnosis, molecular confirmation and treatment; the anaemia and thrombocytopenia are only noted, and the criteria exclude routine case reports with no distinct syndrome or mechanism.
rescue_reason: Single B. gibsoni infection in a pup reports moderate anaemia and severe thrombocytopenia, which are host haematology markers in an infected dog. The rescue rule applies even though the report is a routine single case, and the Babesia-specific host data are clean.

rationale: Cloning of a merozoite antigen and its ELISA performance. There are no host pathophysiological data.

Based on abstract: a treatment comparison in 33 naturally infected dogs that measured haematological values and clinical signs; the full text may give a usable baseline clinicopathological profile, which the abstract does not show.
rescue_reason: Homeopathic versus diminazene trial in infected dogs reports haematological values, which showed no change. Haematology in infected dogs meets the rescue rule even inside a treatment study, so the adjudicator should confirm whether any values are given.

rationale: Based on abstract: experimental infections in dogs that first detected B. gibsoni in host tissues during chronic infection, suggesting sequestration; this is a host-parasite mechanistic observation, beyond the treatment and diagnostic endpoints.
rescue_reason: Experimental B. gibsoni infections report detection of the parasite in tissue during chronic infection, suggesting sequestration. That is a possible host-tissue mechanistic observation, and the adjudicator should check the full text for any host data.

rationale: Tick protein disulfide isomerase genes. B. gibsoni appears only as a tick infection model.
Experimentally infected dogs. Although a treatment study, it reports host data: CRP decreased as PCV recovered, and platelet count was assessed as a marker of treatment response.

species: B. canis and B. rossi (large Babesia)
rationale: Review of vaccine development using soluble parasite antigens. It covers vaccine protection and not host pathophysiology of disease.

species: Various Babesia in animals and ticks (Italy)
rationale: Italian survey of babesial parasites in animals, ticks and people. No host pathophysiological data.

species: B. gibsoni, B. equi, B. microti (parasite and tick)
rationale: Tick antimicrobial peptide (longicin) active against Babesia. It is a vector and parasite study with no dog host data.
Duplicate record of https://openalex.org/W973540217 (same Salvador retrospective study of frequencies by breed and age, with no host pathophysiology).
Phylogeny of Babesia in sheep and goats in China. No dog data.
Serum from infected dogs and culture supernatant suppressed canine reticulocyte maturation in vitro. This is a host-side mechanism for impaired erythropoiesis and anaemia.

species: Babesia sp. (suspected, smear and serology) with Anaplasma platys
rationale: Routine co-infection case report of an imported dog. Babesia was not confirmed by PCR and there are no separable host pathophysiological data.

species: B. canis (unspecified) with E. canis, H. canis and intestinal parasites
rationale: Based on abstract: fatal case in a 6-week-old pup with six concurrent pathogens; the thrombocytopenia, anaemia and hypoproteinaemia are attributed to the multi-pathogen infection, so Babesia-specific host data cannot be separated.
rescue_reason: Fatal multi-pathogen infection in a 6-week-old dog reports severe thrombocytopenia, anaemia and hypoproteinaemia, which are host haematology and biochemistry markers. Babesia canis is one of several co-infections, so the adjudicator must judge whether Babesia-specific host data can be separated.

rationale: Field trial of amitraz collars for preventing tick-borne infection, with PCR detection as the endpoint. No host pathophysiological data.
Review on antibiotic therapy for Lyme disease in people. Babesia appears only as a co-infection and there are no dog babesiosis data.
Patent record for a B. rossi vaccine. It is not peer-reviewed research and has no abstract.

Based on Europe PMC (PMID 16901737): first published online 2006-08-09 (Crossref record created 2006-08-10), before the 2006-10-23 window start; issue date July 2007. The content (45-case clinicopathological and coagulation series) would otherwise be eligible.
Human pulmonary complications case report and review. No dog data.
Prospective study of 95 naturally infected dogs. High cortisol and ACTH and low T4 and free T4 were associated with mortality. This is an endocrine prognostic and outcome study.

species: B. canis vogeli (confirmed, 18S rRNA sequence; experimental)
rationale: Experimental infection of four dogs (two splenectomised) with parasitaemia, PCV, temperature and anaemia follow-up. It reports host responses, and the disease was mild. The molecular characterisation is secondary.
Altered adhesion and mechanical properties of B. bovis-infected bovine red cells. No dog data.
Survey of ticks on dogs and their infection with Babesia and Borrelia. No abstract, but the title shows a tick and vector study with no host pathophysiology.
Human case report of CT and haematological findings. No dog data.

species: Babesia sp. EU1 (roe deer, Ixodes ricinus)
rationale: Culture of Babesia EU1 from roe deer and its transmission in ticks. No dog data.
Survey of microorganisms in tick saliva and midguts in Egypt. No dog host data.
Historical review of human medical parasitology in China. No dog data.
Identification and cloning of an immunodominant parasite antigen with a diagnostic ELISA use. No host pathophysiological data.
Recombinant BgP57 antigen evaluated as an ELISA for diagnosis and serosurvey. No host pathophysiology.
Erratum to a Brazilian perspective paper; no abstract and no data.
Molecular survey of piroplasms in raccoons. No dog data.

species: B. gibsoni P0 antigen / multiple Babesia spp.
rationale: Conserved ribosomal antigen as a vaccine candidate, tested in vitro on B. bovis. No host pathophysiology in dogs.
In vitro screening of plant extracts for antibabesial activity and natural-product chemistry. No host data.
National veterinary drug adverse-reaction report; the piroplasmosis vaccine reactions are in vaccinated dogs, not infected dogs. No pathophysiological data.

species: B. canis canis (confirmed, smear and PCR)
rationale: Based on the abstract (full text paywalled): a descriptive incidence, vector and distribution study whose 13 cases have clinical signs listed only qualitatively, with no haematology or severity analysis. This matches how rounds 1-3 handled surveys with generic clinical-sign lists.
rescue_reason: Lake Geneva canine babesiosis cases (B. canis canis confirmed by PCR) list anaemia, thrombocytopenia and haemoglobinuria as clinical signs. These are qualitative haematology findings in infected dogs, so the exclusion is doubtful and the adjudicator should check the full text.

rationale: Retrospective frequency by breed, age and sex from smear results. No host pathophysiological data.
B. bovis genome sequence; no dog data.

species: Babesia spp. (PCR, mixed with E. canis and A. platys)
rationale: PCR prevalence of E. canis, A. platys and Babesia in thrombocytopenic and non-thrombocytopenic dogs. No separable Babesia-specific host data.
Seroprevalence and risk-factor study of direct transmission in American Pit Bull Terriers. No host pathophysiology.

species: B. canis rossi and B. canis vogeli (confirmed, PCR)
rationale: Molecular prevalence survey in Nigeria. No host data.

Based on the title and record type only (Comment/Letter, no abstract; the publisher page could not be reached). It is a letter on parasite species identity in Brazil, and nothing suggests host pathophysiological data.
rescue_reason: Comment or letter on causative agents of canine babesiosis in Brazil with no abstract. The title does not exclude host clinical data, so the adjudicator should check the full text, which is likely short.

species: none (human and livestock babesiosis; P. falciparum)
rationale: Based on the abstract and MeSH: a review comparing human babesiosis and falciparum malaria pathobiology, with no canine focus and no dog data.
rescue_reason: Review of babesiosis pathobiology (cytokine activation, erythrocyte cytoadherence, organ involvement) that is mainly human and malaria-focused. It describes mechanistic observations in babesiosis, and the scope to canine data should be decided by the adjudicator.

rationale: Molecular survey of vector-borne pathogens in cats.
In vitro cultivation and ultrastructure of the parasite. No host data.
Serological and molecular prevalence survey of tick-borne pathogens in Grenada. No separable host pathophysiological data.
rBgTRAP ELISA developed and evaluated for serodiagnosis. No host pathophysiology.

species: B. canis rossi (naturally infected, virulent babesiosis)
rationale: Prospective study of 94 dogs measuring plasma insulin against glycaemia. It addresses the mechanism of hypoglycaemia, a life-threatening metabolic complication.

species: Babesia sp. (unspecified), mixed with granulocytic ehrlichiosis
rationale: Based on the title, record type (Letter) and MeSH only; the publisher page returned 403. The endpoint is remission of demodicosis after treating concurrent babesiosis and/or ehrlichiosis, with no measured Babesia-specific host pathophysiology, which matches the round-3 exclusion of a demodicosis-babesiosis report.
rescue_reason: Letter with no abstract on demodicosis remission in dogs with concurrent babesiosis and/or ehrlichiosis, possibly retrospective. Host outcome data may exist for Babesia-infected dogs, so the adjudicator should check the full text.

rationale: Serosurvey of horses in Hungary. No dog data.
Histological and ultrastructural renal lesions in 8 dogs that died of B. canis infection. Tubular necrosis is attributed to hypoxic injury, with endothelial change.
Pituitary-adrenal and pituitary-thyroid axis hormones compared across hypoglycaemic, normoglycaemic and hyperglycaemic infected dogs. Endocrine disturbance and its link to glucose perturbations.
ITS sequence discrimination of bovine Babesia. No dog infection data.
ITS1 sequence conservation among isolates. Virulence is discussed only as a genetic hypothesis, with no host data.

species: B. canis canis, vogeli and rossi (PCR)
rationale: Validation of subspecies-specific PCR primers. No host data.

species: B. canis vogeli (confirmed, RLB and sequencing)
rationale: Molecular detection in dogs and ticks in Tunisia. No host pathophysiology.
18S rRNA sequence variants among isolates from symptomatic dogs in Poland. No host data.
Title concerns clinical and laboratory findings in equine piroplasmosis. Not a dog study.
Reference-list entry; the title describes a prevalence and seasonality study, which suggests no host pathophysiological data.

Based on the reconstructed abstract: a short German practitioner-magazine update covering vectors and transmission routes, with no pathophysiology focus. This is consistent with the earlier exclusion of practitioner updates.
rescue_reason: German practitioner update on canine babesiosis (Babesiose/Piroplasmose). The reconstructed abstract covers only vectors and transmission and cannot rule out clinical or pathophysiological content, so the adjudicator should read the full text.

rationale: Human case report of splenic infarction in babesiosis.

species: mouse (B. rodhaini; B. gibsoni antigen only)
rationale: Complement C3 and cross-protective immunity in knockout mice. No dog infection data.

species: B. canis (serology, mixed with Leishmania and E. canis)
rationale: Serological cross-reactivity study (IFAT and ELISA). No host pathophysiology.

species: B. canis vogeli (PCR) within a mixed other-vector-borne group; E. canis focus
rationale: Based on the abstract (Wiley PDF returned 403): the study is about cardiac injury in E. canis infection, and Babesia-positive dogs sit inside a pooled other-vector-borne group with no Babesia-specific results reported. Mixed infections without separable Babesia data are excluded.
rescue_reason: Cardiac troponin I, anaemia severity and SIRS in E. canis-infected dogs. The Babesia canis vogeli PCR-positive dogs sit in a mixed vector-borne group, so the adjudicator should check whether Babesia-specific data can be separated in the full text.

rationale: Polish narrative review of canine babesiosis clinical signs, haematology (anaemia, leucopenia, thrombocytopenia) and biochemistry (AST, ALT, bilirubin, urea, creatinine), with a note on subspecies differences in severity.
Human case report of babesiosis presenting as fever of unknown origin.

species: none (Rickettsia spp., human cases and ticks)
rationale: Spotted fever rickettsioses in humans and Rhipicephalus sanguineus behaviour; no Babesia-infected dog data.

species: Babesia sp. (suspected, farmed wolf Canis lupus)
rationale: Canis lupus counts as canine, but this is a routine single case (depression, haematuria, antibiotic treatment) with no distinct syndrome or mechanistic observation.
Cross-sectional survey of ectoparasites and haemoparasites in 57 dogs; no host pathophysiological data.
Serological and PCR survey of vector-borne parasites in Albania and Kosovo; prevalence only.
No abstract; the title indicates parasite molecular diversity with no sign of host data, so it does not suggest eligible content.
Blood parasite prevalence in stray and pet dogs and a microfilaria technique comparison; no host pathophysiology.
102 naturally infected dogs with clinical scores, haemoglobin range, jaundice and haemoglobinuria findings and case fatality: a multisystem clinical phenotype and severity profile.

species: B. canis and B. gibsoni (suspected, smear) mixed with E. canis
rationale: Based on the abstract: this is a single pup with B. canis, B. gibsoni and E. canis triple infection, and E. canis can also cause respiratory signs, so the diffuse lung disease and anaemia cannot be attributed to Babesia. A one-dog report cannot separate Babesia-specific host data, and the report focuses on management and treatment.
rescue_reason: Case report of respiratory distress with radiographically confirmed diffuse lung disease, plus anaemia, in a Great Dane pup with B. canis and B. gibsoni co-infection. This may be a distinct pulmonary syndrome, and the Ehrlichia co-infection limits attribution, so the adjudicator should check whether Babesia-specific host data can be separated (full text).

rationale: Gene cloning and recombinant antigen characterisation, with a diagnostic angle; no host pathophysiology.
Serum LTB4 and PGE2 in 26 dogs with acute babesiosis against 17 controls; eicosanoid inflammatory mediators in the host.

species: B. vogeli and B. gibsoni (confirmed, PCR-RFLP)
rationale: Based on the full text (Redalyc PDF; RBPV 17 Suppl 1:277-283, full article): 282 hospital dogs with cytopenias were screened by PCR. The paper tabulates anaemia, thrombocytopenia and leukopenia patterns in PCR-positive vs PCR-negative dogs and by species, so this survey also reports haematology of infected dogs.
rescue_reason: Occurrence and molecular characterisation of Babesia in a hospital dog population, with a truncated abstract. The title suggests a molecular survey, but the abstract cannot rule out haematology or clinical data from hospital cases, so the adjudicator should check the full text.

species: B. rossi (PCR/RLB, African wild dog Lycaon pictus)
rationale: Molecular detection in African wild dogs, a non-Canis canid, with no domestic dog data; it is also a prevalence survey.

species: B. canis canis (PCR) and Theileria spp.
rationale: Veterinary doctoral thesis (the abstract says 'travail de these'). It does report haematology of PCR-positive dogs, but theses are excluded.

Based on the journal summary page (Bajer et al., Med Weter 64(4):441-443, 2008): splenomegaly from presumed chronic asymptomatic B. canis infection led to splenic rupture and splenectomy, and clinical babesiosis followed the surgery. This is a distinct splenic complication, consistent with earlier splenopathy case inclusions.
Review of brown dog tick taxonomy, ecology and control; no host data.

species: Babesia sp. (suspected, smear) only in triple co-infection with Hepatozoon and Ehrlichia
rationale: Based on the abstract: this is a Hepatozoon study. All 26 Babesia-positive dogs also carried Hepatozoon and Ehrlichia, and there is no Babesia-only group, so no Babesia-specific host data can be separated.
rescue_reason: Retrospective study of 115 dogs with Hepatozoon infection, reporting clinical signs and haematology (anaemia, leukocytosis, neutrophilia, left shift). Its 26-dog Babesia/Hepatozoon/Ehrlichia subgroup may have Babesia-specific host data that a separate analysis can recover, so the adjudicator should check the full text.

rationale: Reply/letter ('Re:') on an epidemiological paper, with no abstract or data.
Human case-control study of persistent B. microti infection in immunocompromised patients; no dog data.
Parasite Hsp70 expression under temperature stress in culture; no host data.

species: B. gibsoni (in vivo and in vitro)
rationale: Flow cytometry method to measure parasitaemia, using one infected dog and cultures; no host pathophysiology.

Title only: OpenAlex has no abstract, and web and Europe PMC searches did not find one (Beelitz et al., Kleintierpraxis 53, 2008). An update on B. canis infections in dogs in southern Germany may describe clinical and laboratory findings of cases or may be purely epidemiological, so eligibility cannot be judged without the full text.
rescue_reason: German practitioner article ('Aktuelles zu Babesia-canis-Infektionen') with no abstract. The title does not rule out a clinical review with haematology or clinical picture, so the adjudicator should check the full text.

rationale: Pathogen prevalence in ticks removed from dogs; no host data.

Based on the title and Crossref metadata; no abstract was reachable because the publisher link (metapress) is defunct. This is an 11-page case report (Pomianowski et al., Pol J Nat Sci 23(1):257-267, 2008) of B. canis-associated acute renal failure needing peritoneal dialysis, a distinct renal complication that earlier rounds included.
A case report of an unusual presentation with neurological signs and pancytopenia that resolved with treatment: a distinct syndrome (cerebral involvement).
Review of human babesiosis phylogeny, diagnostics and treatment; no canine pathophysiology.
Piroplasm detected in a rhesus macaque; no dog data.
Avian piroplasm molecular characterisation; no dog data.
Frequency of infection by smear in 2,031 dogs; prevalence only.
Adrenal function (basal and ACTH-stimulated cortisol, cortisol-to-ACTH ratio) in 68 infected dogs against controls, related to outcome.
Erythrocytic antioxidant enzymes, lipid peroxides and blood iron, zinc and copper in infected dogs against healthy controls; oxidative damage linked to anaemia.
First detection of infection in stray dogs by an immunochromatographic test; no host pathophysiology.

species: B. rossi, B. vogeli, Theileria sp. (PCR/RLB)
rationale: Molecular survey of tick-borne pathogens in 1,138 dogs; no host data.
Human case of splenic rupture in B. microti infection.
DNA extraction from dried blood spots and comparison of four PCR methods; no host data.

Title only: OpenAlex has no abstract (Indian Vet J 85(10):1037-1039). This is a short comparative drug-efficacy note, and earlier rounds excluded title-only drug comparisons such as imidocarb vs diminazene as treatment_efficacy. Nothing indicates mechanistic or host-pathophysiology outcomes.
rescue_reason: Comparative efficacy of clindamycin and diminazine in canine babesiosis, with no abstract. Treatment trials often report haematology (for example PCV or haemoglobin) in infected dogs, and the title does not rule that out, so the adjudicator should check the full text.

rationale: Nationwide serosurvey and risk factors; no host pathophysiology.
Tick cysteine protease (longipain) and its effect on Babesia in the vector; no host data.
No abstract; the title (seasonal occurrence and local climate) indicates an epidemiology study with no host pathophysiology.

species: none (B. microti-like, Ixodes persulcatus and mice)
rationale: Rodent-type Babesia isolated from ticks in China; no dog data.

species: B. canis (7 dogs) and B. vogeli (1 dog) (confirmed, PCR and sequencing)
rationale: Based on the abstract: a PCR-confirmed clinical case series of 8 dogs reporting clinical signs (pallor, haemoglobinuria, hyperthermia, tremors) but no haematology. The full text (Vet Parasitol 156:199-204) may give per-dog clinicopathological data, which cannot be checked behind access control.
rescue_reason: Molecular characterisation of B. canis canis and B. canis vogeli in eight clinically suspected dogs. The abstract lists clinical signs (pale mucous membranes, red urine, tremors, weight loss, hyperthermia) in a small case series, with no haematology given. The full text may report haematology, so the adjudicator should check it.

species: B. canis, B. microti, B. divergens (review; diagnostics)
rationale: Review of molecular (PCR) diagnostics for human and canine babesiosis, with no host pathophysiological data.
Sheep infected with Babesia ovis; no dog data.

species: B. gibsoni co-infection with E. chaffeensis in one dog (confirmed, PCR)
rationale: Based on the abstract: the case report is about Ehrlichia chaffeensis. The single B. gibsoni co-infected dog's haematuria and thrombocytopenia cannot be separated from the ehrlichiosis, so no Babesia-specific host data are available.
rescue_reason: Case report of Ehrlichia chaffeensis in dogs. One dog is co-infected with B. gibsoni and has haematuria and thrombocytopenia. B. microti antigen and serodiagnosis; no dog data.

species: B. rossi and B. vogeli (review; no primary data)

Based on the abstract: a routine single case of icterus with hyperbilirubinaemia, diagnosed by smear and treated. Hyperbilirubinaemia is an expected finding, not a distinct syndrome or mechanistic observation, so the rescue is not upheld.

species: B. canis sensu lato (suspected, smear only)

The abstract does not show whether PCV is reported for Babesia-infected dogs separately, so the full text must decide.

Based on the full text (DOI landing PDF, Vet World 2011;4(6):269-270, online 2011-03-25): a routine single case of severe anaemia (Hb 3 g/dl, PCV 20%) diagnosed by smear and treated with diminazene, oxytetracycline and transfusion. It describes no distinct syndrome or mechanistic observation.
Summary of a virology society meeting; unrelated to canine Babesia.
Splenic cell dynamics in calves infected with B. bovis; no dog data.
Human case of stress cardiomyopathy in severe babesiosis; no dog data.
Laboratory detection rates for several vector-borne pathogens in imported dogs; no host pathophysiological data.
Molecular detection of Hepatozoon and Babesia in 10 dogs; no host data.
Breed and sex risk-factor analysis of hospital cases; no host pathophysiological data.
Case report of protein-losing nephropathy with membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis and immune complex deposition on histopathology, a distinct renal syndrome with a mechanistic observation.
PCR prevalence of Babesia, Bartonella and Mycoplasma DNA in archived spleens of dogs with splenic disease; no host pathophysiology of babesiosis.
Phylogenetic characterisation of 18S rRNA sequences from Brazilian isolates; no host data.
Serum protein electrophoresis in infected dogs with globulin fraction changes attributed to haemolysis, complement and dehydration; a host clinicopathological and acute-phase profile.

From the abstract and title: a case series of 18 clinical cases whose title promises haemato-biochemical data, which would make it an eligible clinicopathological profile, but the abstract gives only clinical signs and treatment response. From the abstract: a routine single case of haemolytic jaundice with hyperbilirubinaemia, diagnosis and recovery after treatment, which is the expected presentation, with no distinct syndrome or mechanistic observation. Rounds 1-3 excluded such cases the same way; the case-report rule applies, not a host-marker rescue.
rescue_reason: Reports jaundice with hyperbilirubinaemia, a hepatic biochemical marker, in a dog with babesiosis. The host-marker rescue rule applies even though the case is routine.

rationale: From the title and OpenAlex metadata (no abstract; the publisher landing page is dead): a case report of ARDS due to babesiosis in a dog, and ARDS is a distinct syndrome named in the case-report inclusion rule. Repository copy (University of Nairobi) of the same paper by Aleri, Mulei, Mande et al.; duplicate record of https://openalex.org/W2232812342.
Prevalence survey of canine parasites; no host pathophysiological data.

From the title only (Nig Vet J 32(2):69-78; no abstract, and the AJOL page did not load): a general status review of canine babesiosis that may cover pathogenesis and clinical syndromes, or only Nigerian epidemiology. Full text is needed to judge its scope.
Molecular and microscopic survey in the Philippines with all samples negative; no host data.
Prevalence of haemoprotozoan infection in stray dogs; no host data.

From the title and OpenAlex metadata only (Scientific Works Series C Vet Med 57(2):276-282; CAB record withdrawn, no abstract): a clinic-based study of canine babesiosis that could be a clinicopathological series or an epidemiological summary. Eligibility cannot be judged without the full text.
Seasonal prevalence of canine babesiosis in Lahore; no host pathophysiology.

species: B. canis (infected dogs, species method not stated)
rationale: ALT, AST and ALP activities in 230 infected dogs with and without anaemia, addressing hepatic enzyme changes and the effect of anaemia. Treated as a new record despite the retired ID CB029.

From the title and OpenAlex metadata (Research Journal of Animal Sciences 5(2); no abstract): a case report of ARDS due to babesiosis in a dog, a distinct syndrome that meets the case-report rule. This is the journal version; W1169740358 is a repository duplicate of it.
18S rRNA sequence identification of the parasite from one dog; no host data.
Molecular identification and phylogeny of B. vogeli from pet dogs in China; no host data.

From the abstract: a routine single case of diagnosis and cure, where the paralysis comes from the tick (Haemaphysalis longicornis) and not from babesiosis. rescue_reason: Single case of tick paralysis with B. gibsoni infection that reports low haemoglobin (anaemia, ERY) in an infected dog. The haematology finding meets the host-marker rule even though the case is routine.

rationale: Diploma thesis on molecular detection of Babesia in questing ticks; not peer reviewed and has no dog data.

From the title only (no abstract; the CAB record is withdrawn): an IFA seroprevalence survey of B. canis in dogs from the Banat region. Rounds 1-3 excluded seroprevalence surveys like this, and nothing suggests host pathophysiological data.
rescue_reason: No abstract. The title is an IFA epidemiosurvey of B. canis in dogs, which does not rule out host data in seropositive dogs; check the full text.

rationale: From the title only (no abstract; the CAB record is withdrawn): a prevalence comparison of Babesia infection in rural and urban dogs in Ahvaz. This is a pure epidemiological survey, and nothing indicates host pathophysiological data.
rescue_reason: No abstract. The title is a prevalence survey of Babesia in rural and urban dogs, which does not rule out host data; check the full text.

rationale: From the title and OpenAlex metadata (Mayer, Kis, Stokovic, Bendelja, Mrljak; CROSBI record 556443, which sits behind a bot check, so there is no abstract): measuring host cytokines TNF-alpha, IL-6 and IL-10 in B. canis-infected dogs is squarely on topic. From the abstract and the Fiocruz repository record (journal article, Rev Bras Med Vet 33, 2011): a prevalence and tick-exposure survey in which clinical signs (splenomegaly, weight loss) are reported only in aggregate across single and mixed Babesia/Ehrlichia infections. rescue_reason: Abstract reports clinical signs in Babesia-infected dogs (splenomegaly, progressive weight loss) and a Babesia-dominant infection subgroup, so host clinical data are present and partly separable.

rationale: Distribution of the tick vector in western Poland; no dog data.

rescue_reason: Reports higher rectal temperature in Babesia-positive dogs, a host physiological and inflammatory-type marker in infected dogs. The first screener's view that it is not pathophysiological is disputed.

Serum urea, creatinine, urea:creatinine ratio and GFR in dogs with babesiosis compared with IMHA, controls and experimental haemoglobinaemia, addressing renal function and the effect of haemolysis.

Human babesiosis case in a boy with a general review; the dog is mentioned only as the source and has no host data.
Risk-factor and distribution analysis of canine babesiosis in Poland; no host pathophysiological data.

The Texas B. canis rossi dog had nonregenerative anaemia, neutropenia, thrombocytopenia and azotaemia, which is a clinicopathological profile. It is a single case, so the adjudicator should weigh the case-report threshold.

species: Babesia sp. in sheep and goats

Structural biology of a B. bovis enzyme. No dog data.

Oxidative stress in ovine babesiosis. No dog data.

species: B. canis and B. vogeli (confirmed, PCR)

species: B. canis canis (confirmed, PCR and sequencing)

species: B. microti (experimental inoculation; confirmed by PCR and IFA)

From the abstract: a treatment trial in 30 naturally infected dogs that recorded haematological parameters at presentation and during treatment, but the abstract reports no values. The full text may give a clinicopathological profile of infected dogs, so it should be checked at full-text review.

rationale: Characterises recombinant merozoite surface antigens for serodiagnosis (ELISA); no host pathophysiological data.

rationale: Tick survey of Dermacentor reticulatus in Belgium; no dog host data.

Nationwide questionnaire on the number of B. gibsoni cases; no host pathophysiological data.
PCR survey of Babesia in questing ticks in Serbia; no dog data.

species: Leishmania infantum (B. canis only as cross-reaction serum)

Gliding motility of B. bovis merozoites in bovine erythrocytes; no dog data.

Parasite survey of wild and domestic canids; Babesia is mentioned only as seropositivity, with no host data.

species: B. canis (infected dogs; method not stated in abstract)

Protein fractions of culture-derived soluble antigen and their immunoreactivity with sera from vaccinated dogs; vaccine antigen work with no data from infected dogs.

species: B. canis (infected dogs; method not stated in abstract)
rationale: Reports the SUSPPUP ratio and fractional excretion of electrolytes in hospitalised dogs. It suggests mineralocorticoid excess and tubular necrosis in azotaemic dogs.
Human Lyme disease and co-infection review; no dog data.
Haematology and biochemistry of small ruminants with B. ovis; not a canine host.
Morphometry of piroplasms on blood smears; no host pathophysiological data.

From the abstract: PCR subspecies identification in three clinical cases from northern India. It reports no host haematological or pathophysiological findings, and it describes routine cases that show no distinct syndrome.
rescue_reason: Abstract is very short and describes three clinically affected dogs, and the title does not rule out host data. The routine-case exclusion is likely right, but the full text should be checked for haematology or other host findings.

species: B. gibsoni and B. canis (smear only)
rationale: From the abstract: a smear-based prevalence survey of blood and gut parasites in dogs in Ludhiana. Here 'haematological investigation' means blood-smear examination, and no host values or comparisons are reported.
rescue_reason: Haematological investigations were done on 460 dogs, of whom 8.26% were B. gibsoni positive. The abstract gives no values, so host haematology for infected dogs may be in the full text. Rescued liberally; the adjudicator should check.

rationale: From the abstract: a detection survey (16/103 pet dogs in Xi'an) with a monthly distribution. Its clinical signs are a generic description of the disease, and it reports no haematology or biochemistry results for the infected dogs.
rescue_reason: Abstract describes clinical characteristics (fever, anaemia, haemoglobinuria, splenic swelling) and blood tests for 16 infected pet dogs. The clinical data may hold host findings, so the full text should be checked.

rationale: Development of a PCR assay for canine Babesia; no host data.

species: Babesia spp. (review; B. canis canis focus likely)
rationale: Title and OpenAlex metadata only; no abstract was reachable. It is a narrative review of canine babesiosis by the Zagreb Mrljak group (Veterinarska stanica 43(6):497-505, 2012), whose work centres on pathogenesis and complications, so it is included as a review, with a full-text check of scope.
No abstract, but the title states epidemiological aspects of B. c. vogeli in dogs in Baixada Fluminense, which points to a prevalence study.

Title and OpenAlex metadata only; the CROSBI/CroRIS landing page is behind a bot check. It is a Mrljak-group study of glutathione peroxidase in the pathogenesis of B. canis canis infection, which would be eligible oxidative-stress evidence, but the 'Zbornik radova' source (first page 389) suggests conference proceedings, so peer-review status must be checked at full text.

species: B. canis (naturally infected; diagnostic method not stated)
rationale: Serial lipid profile (cholesterol, HDL, LDL, triglycerides) in 26 infected dogs versus 17 healthy dogs on days 1, 3 and 7, framed within the acute-phase response.
No abstract, but the title describes tick infestation and prevalence in El-Tarf, Algeria.

species: Hepatozoon canis; B. canis co-infection in 1/8 dogs (smear)
rationale: From the abstract: a Hepatozoon canis case series, in which the haematology is pooled across eight dogs. Only one dog had a B. canis co-infection, so no Babesia-specific host data can be separated.
rescue_reason: Canine case series reports haematology (anaemia, thrombocytopaenia, leucocytosis) in dogs, one of which had B. canis co-infection. Babesia-specific data cannot be separated, so the adjudicator should decide, but the exclusion reason is questionable.

rationale: Title and OpenAlex metadata only (Guerra, Ardila and López, Universidad del Tolima repository, pp. 91-99, 2012); the repository page is behind a bot check. A case report of nephrotic syndrome would be a distinct renal syndrome, but the diagnosis, the evidence, the peer-review status and the original publication date cannot be checked.
Duplicate record of DOI:10.12935/jvma.65.293, a nationwide questionnaire on the number of B. gibsoni cases with no host pathophysiology.

species: B. vogeli and B. gibsoni (PCR, among other pathogens)
rationale: Doctoral thesis on canine vector-borne diseases in India. It is a prevalence study, and its PCV comparison pools all pathogens.
No abstract. The title shows a comparison of DNA isolation methods for real-time PCR sensitivity.
Atovaquone with azithromycin treatment, with PCR clearance as the endpoint. It also reports re-emergence of the species but gives no host pathophysiological data.
Review on the pathophysiology of canine babesiosis and the diversity of disease manifestations across European countries, which fits the review scope.

species: Babesia spp. in ticks (not dog host data)
rationale: Molecular survey of pathogens in ticks from cattle and dogs, with no host pathophysiology.
PCR detection of B. vogeli in 12 dogs and in ticks in southern France; it reports occurrence only, with no host clinicopathological data.
Structure and erythrocyte-binding function of a merozoite surface protein, with no host-side data from infected dogs.
Human obstetric anaesthesia case report.

species: B. bovis in cattle and buffalo
rationale: Ruminant study; dogs appear only as a herd risk factor.
Tick survey from cattle in Turkey; no dog data.

species: Theileria equi and B. caballi in horses
rationale: Equine seroprevalence survey.
Human case report in a patient on a TNF-alpha antagonist.

species: B. equi and B. caballi in horses
rationale: Equine piroplasmosis outbreak investigation.

species: Babesia sp. in a maned wolf (Chrysocyon brachyurus; PCR)
rationale: Case in a maned wolf, a non-Canis canid, with no dog data.

species: B. canis canis in Dermacentor reticulatus ticks
rationale: The title shows a prevalence study of B. canis in ticks from the Saarland, so it is a vector survey. No abstract is available, but the title is clear.

species: B. vogeli (confirmed, PCR and serology); mixed with A. platys
rationale: Abstract: a single co-infected dog whose thrombocytopenia, anaemia and raised CRP cannot be attributed to B. vogeli rather than A. platys, and the report centres on the first detection of A. platys. It describes no Babesia-specific distinct syndrome or mechanistic observation.
rescue_reason: Case report in a dog with A. platys and B. vogeli co-infection that reports thrombocytopenia, anaemia and raised CRP. The exclusion as routine diagnosis looks wrong, but the haematology cannot be separated by parasite, so the adjudicator should judge whether Babesia-specific host data exist.

rationale: Abstract: experimental R. vitalii infection with changes in serum copper, iron and zinc. Rangelia is a separate piroplasm genus outside the canine Babesia scope, the same ruling as the round-1 Rangelia records (for example PMID:28902259).
18S rRNA phylogeny of piroplasmids, with no host data.
First human babesiosis case in Australia.
Practice recommendations covering many canine vector-borne diseases, with no babesiosis pathophysiology content.
Development of a real-time PCR to differentiate subspecies and its use in a prevalence survey, with no host pathophysiology.

species: Piroplasmid DNA (T. equi, B. caballi) in stray dogs
rationale: PCR survey of hemopathogens and ticks in stray dogs in Jordan, with no host pathophysiological data.

Abstract: platelet counts and purinergic enzyme activities in dogs experimentally infected with R. vitalii. Rangelia is a separate piroplasm genus outside the canine Babesia scope, as ruled for Rangelia records in round 1, even though the host data are mechanistic.
Serum monovalent electrolyte and ion-gap disturbances in 70 B. canis dogs, compared by azotaemia and anaemia status; this is an acid-base and electrolyte pathophysiology study.

species: B. canis (suspected, smear); mixed with Ehrlichia spp. and Neospora caninum serology
rationale: Abstract (OpenAlex, reconstructed): a single case report focused on diagnosing concurrent infections, with no laboratory values and no distinct syndrome or mechanistic observation. With three pathogens, Babesia-specific host data could not be separated even if the full text has a haemogram.
rescue_reason: Brazilian case report of concurrent Neospora, B. canis and Ehrlichia infection, with an abstract that refers to laboratory findings but gives no values. The full text may include a haemogram, so the adjudicator should check it; mixed infection limits separation of Babesia-specific data.

rationale: PCR prevalence survey of canine vector-borne pathogens in Australian dogs, with no host pathophysiology.
Coxiella symbiont in soft ticks; Babesia was not detected and there are no dog data.

species: B. vogeli (smear) in 2 of 14 dogs; mostly Hepatozoon canis
rationale: Abstract: the syndrome is tick paralysis attributed to R. sanguineus toxin, not babesiosis. Only 2 of 14 dogs had B. vogeli, mixed with H. canis, and the haematology is not reported by parasite, so there are no separable Babesia-specific host data.
rescue_reason: Tick paralysis syndrome in 14 dogs infested with R. sanguineus, with thrombocytopenia, hypoalbuminaemia and pancytopenia reported in infected dogs; two dogs also had B. vogeli. The haematology cannot be assigned to Babesia, so the adjudicator should decide whether it counts, but the distinct syndrome means exclusion as other_out_of_scope is doubtful.

rationale: Review of tick cystatins in tick physiology; it mentions B. gibsoni only for tick innate immunity.

Haematological profile of 113 B. canis-infected dogs, reporting thrombocytopenia, anaemia, reticulocyte response and leukopenia. This clinicopathological profile counts as descriptive host evidence even though the aim is diagnostic.

species: African wild dog (Lycaon pictus); Babesia not detected
rationale: Pathogen exposure survey in wild dogs, a non-Canis canid, where Babesia was never detected.
Review of parasite and red cell molecules in invasion, framed for human babesiosis, with no dog data.
Ovine Babesia ELISA and serosurvey.

species: B. canis (detection method unknown; blood smear/18S PCR per metadata); with T. annulata
rationale: Title and metadata only: the doi.org/Springer page needs sign-in, OpenAlex has no abstract and Europe PMC has no record. It is a 3-page Comparative Clinical Pathology report (Bigdeli et al., 2012, Iran) that may contain haematology of infected dogs, so eligibility cannot be judged without the full text.
PCR and serology prevalence survey of haemoparasites in free-roaming dogs, with no host pathophysiological data.
Mitochondrial genes and diminazene resistance in cultured B. gibsoni, with no host data.
QT prolongation with quinidine in human patients.
Survey of the parasite cytochrome b gene for atovaquone-resistance mutations in 92 samples, with no host data.
News item on the first human babesiosis case in Australia; it mentions canine babesiosis only as background.

species: B. canis canis soluble antigen vaccine (uninfected dogs)
rationale: Vaccine safety study in uninfected dogs. The haematology and biochemistry are vaccine reactions, not host data from infected dogs.
Human case report of babesiosis with Borrelia co-infection.
Seroprevalence and risk factors in 197 healthy dogs in Romania, with no pathophysiology.
Review of human babesiosis (NEJM); no abstract, and the title and MeSH terms show a human focus.
Development of an immunochromatographic test using recombinant BgTRAP; reports only sensitivity and specificity, no host pathophysiology.
PCR survey and phylogeny in 102 asymptomatic dogs; no host pathophysiological data.
Cloning and immunological characterisation of B. bigemina HSP70 with a mouse B. microti model; no dog data.
Pathogen co-occurrence in questing ticks from Serbia; no dog host data.
Hospital disease-prevalence survey of pet dogs in Bangladesh in which babesiosis is one listed condition (0.08%); no host pathophysiology.
Human babesiosis surveillance report from the United States; no dog data.
Molecular detection in lions, leopards and cheetahs; no dog data.
Case of E. muris infection in a dog; the dog was Babesia-seronegative and no Babesia data are reported.
Genome sequencing of the human pathogen B. microti; no dog host data.

species: B. rossi (virulent canine babesiosis, South Africa)
rationale: NT-proBNP and cTnI measured in 45 babesiosis dogs of three severity grades versus 15 controls, with echocardiographic and renal/lactate data; a cardiac biomarker and severity study.
Urinary IgG, CRP and RBP show glomerular and tubular dysfunction in dogs with uncomplicated B. rossi infection versus healthy dogs; this is host renal pathophysiology.
Review of Babesia taxonomy, phylogeny and evolution with emphasis on human-infecting species; no host pathophysiology in dogs.
Case of vertical transmission of B. microti in a human infant; no dog data.
Multiplex serological assay for B. microti IgG in human sera; no dog data.
In vitro energy and glycolysis metabolism of diminazene-resistant B. gibsoni isolates; parasite-side data only.
Overview of vectors and vector-borne zoonoses in Vojvodina; mentions piroplasmosis only in passing, with no host pathophysiological data.
Lipid peroxidation and antioxidant enzymes in goats infected with B. ovis; no dog data.
qPCR parasite burden in the vector tick H. longicornis ovaries and eggs; no host pathophysiology.
Species and pathogen detection in ticks removed from dogs versus questing ticks; no host data.
Mouse developmental lead and stress neurotoxicology; unrelated to Babesia.

species: B. canis, B. vogeli, B. gibsoni, T. annae (confirmed, RLB)
rationale: Reverse line blot assay for canine piroplasms and co-infections; it reports species identification and co-infection only, with no host pathophysiology.
Survey of PCR, microscopy and serology prevalence in Slovak dogs; no host pathophysiological data.

species: Babesia sp. NV-1 in mink (not canine)
rationale: Molecular detection of a Babesia in American mink; no dog data.
PCR detection of vector-borne pathogens in ticks and 23 dog blood samples in Kiev; occurrence only, with no host pathophysiology.

Based on the abstract from the journal landing page: a PCR prevalence and risk-factor survey of 300 dogs (10 positive) and R. sanguineus ticks in Maranhão. The only host data are age, breed, sex and tick control as risk factors, with no haematology or clinical data.
rescue_reason: No abstract, and the title is a molecular detection study of B. canis vogeli in dogs and R. sanguineus. Detection studies of this kind often report haematology of positive dogs, so the record cannot be ruled out without the full text; route to the adjudicator.

rationale: Imported human B. microti infection in Australia; no dog data.

Title and PubMed metadata only. There is no abstract, and the AVMA landing page returned 403. It is a 'Pathology in practice' clinicopathological case from NC State (Birkenheuer), and it cannot be judged whether it describes a distinct syndrome or a routine diagnosis, so it goes to full-text review.
Presumptive cerebral babesiosis with neurological signs and pancytopenia, with brain histopathology and PCR post mortem; a distinct cerebral syndrome with mechanistic findings.
Prospective study of 72 dogs showing that non-survivors had a more severe consumptive coagulopathy (low factors and protein C, high D-dimer); a mortality and mechanism study.

Based on the abstract. This is a tick-transmission-blocking collar trial, and its endpoints are transmission, tick mortality and infection status. For the control dogs, the abstract reports only that clinical signs occurred, that the dogs seroconverted and that they were PCR-positive, which confirms infection but gives no pathophysiological data, so the rescue does not change the decision.
rescue_reason: Abstract reports that all control dogs experimentally infected with B. canis developed clinical signs of babesiosis, specific IFA antibodies and PCR/RLB positivity. These are host responses in infected dogs in an experimental infection, so the vector_tick exclusion looks wrong.

rationale: Babesia detection in ticks collected from police dogs in China; no host data.
Seroprevalence of four tick-borne pathogens in kennelled dogs in Italy; no host pathophysiology.
Cloning of B. gibsoni IMPDH and its inhibition by mycophenolic acid in vitro; parasite-side drug target work.
Seroprevalence of tick-borne infections in Korean military dogs; no Babesia-positive dogs and no host data.

species: B. canis (confirmed, PCR in ticks only)
rationale: Based on the abstract. B. canis was detected only in 2 D. marginatus ticks, and infection of the host dogs was not established. The clinical and laboratory abnormalities are described only as the enrolment reason for all 22 dogs, so there are no Babesia-specific host data.
rescue_reason: Babesia canis was detected in ticks removed from dogs with clinical signs and laboratory abnormalities compatible with tick-borne disease, so host data on the Babesia-exposed dogs may exist. Abstract does not separate them, so route to the adjudicator. Vector_tick exclusion is questionable.

rationale: Thromboelastography, PT, aPTT, fibrinogen and antithrombin in 19 dogs with uncomplicated babesiosis versus 10 controls, showing a normocoagulable state despite severe thrombocytopenia.

species: Babesia sp. (suspected, smear only); mixed cohort with Ehrlichia
rationale: Based on the abstract (OpenAlex and the publisher landing page). It reports thrombocytopenia, platelet aggregates and giant platelets in dogs with Babesia or Ehrlichia, but the landing page gives no methods, so it is unknown whether the Babesia dogs are reported separately. Full-text review is needed.

species: B. canis (infection in 23 dogs; method not stated in abstract)
rationale: Euthyroid sick syndrome in 23 dogs with B. canis: decreased TT4 and FT4, correlated with urea and creatinine in azotaemic and non-azotaemic dogs; an endocrine disturbance.

species: B. canis (serology; Babesia sp. PCR in 2 spleens); co-infected with E. canis and L. chagasi
rationale: Based on the UNESP repository landing page (handle 11449/96002). It is a 2012 Master's dissertation, and the journal attribution in OpenAlex is wrong. Its abstract also reports only serological and PCR detection, with no Babesia-specific host data.
Prevalence of Babesia in stray dogs in Baghdad by region, season and sex; no host pathophysiology.
In vitro acaricide test on ticks with no dog host data.
Retrospective prevalence study of haemoprotozoa in dogs; the abstract reports no host pathophysiological data.

species: B. canis canis (confirmed, smear and PCR)
rationale: This is a duplicate record of PMID:17983018 (Porchet et al., Schweiz Arch Tierheilkd 2007;149:457-65; the original publication is inside the window, and OpenAlex shows a later deposit date). The full abstract from PubMed lists clinicopathological findings (anaemia, thrombocytopenia, haemoglobinuria) in 13 confirmed cases, but the study is mainly epidemiological, so it goes to full text to check how much case-level data it reports. Give it the same decision as PMID:17983018.
rescue_reason: The abstract is truncated mid-sentence and describes a case-listing study of canine babesiosis cases in the Lake Geneva region. Clinicopathological data may be present, so the full abstract or landing page must be checked (low confidence).

rationale: Based on the abstract (PubMed): a first molecular report of E. canis and A. platys in which the haematology belongs to the rickettsial study. B. vogeli appears only as a documented co-infection, with no Babesia-specific host data that can be separated out.
rescue_reason: The abstract reports haematological findings in dogs with E. canis and A. platys and documents B. vogeli co-infection. Babesia-specific haematology may be separable in the full text, so this is a mixed-infection case to check.

rationale: Novel Babesia in eastern grey kangaroos; no dog data.
Title concerns erythrocyte antioxidant mechanisms in bovine babesiosis; the host is cattle.
Duplicate record of DOI:10.3906/vet-1201-45; the title indicates a molecular first-detection report with no pathophysiological content.

species: B. canis (confirmed on blood smear, 226 dogs)
rationale: Treatment comparison that also reports clinical findings, haematology and urinalysis of 226 infected dogs before and after treatment (anaemia, haemoglobinuria); this host data meets the inclusion rule for treatment studies.
Routine case report of first molecular detection in two dogs with no haematology or mechanistic data.

species: Ehrlichia canis (Babesia only as negative cross-reactivity control)
rationale: LAMP assay development for E. canis; Babesia samples serve only as specificity controls.

species: Babesia sp. (suspected, smear only; mostly mixed with Anaplasma)
rationale: Based on the abstract: lower PCV and Hb are reported in infected dogs, but most were mixed Babesia/Anaplasma infections. The open-access PDF could not be parsed, so it is unclear whether Babesia-only haematology can be separated out; check at full text.
Smear-based prevalence survey with no host pathophysiological data.

species: B. canis (experimental infection of a splenectomised dog)
rationale: Based on the landing page (SCIRP): a study of Bm86 vaccination and co-feeding transmission in ticks. The only host data are incidental parasitaemia, fever and a haematocrit drop in a single splenectomised donor dog used to infect ticks, so there is no host-pathophysiology aim or usable dataset.
rescue_reason: No abstract. The title describes ticks fed on dogs vaccinated with Bm86 and infected with Babesia canis. The experimental dog infection could report host responses (antibodies, parasitaemia or haematology), which the title does not rule out.

species: B. canis canis (confirmed, smear and PCR)
rationale: Based on the OpenAlex abstract (the publisher PDF was unreachable): a three-dog case series with clinical, haematological and biochemical findings in complicated babesiosis (haemolytic anaemia, haemoglobinuria, thrombocytopenia, hepatopathy, myositis, cholecystitis, renal injury) and one death, which describes distinct complications.
Review of the transmission and epidemiology of zoonotic protozoa in pets; its subject is not canine babesiosis pathophysiology.

species: B. vogeli and B. gibsoni (confirmed, PCR and sequencing)
rationale: Based on the PMC full text: alongside the prevalence data, the paper reports clinical status and CBC/biochemistry for dogs with single B. vogeli (n=12) and single B. gibsoni (n=12) infections (mostly subclinical, with occasional anaemia, thrombocytopenia, leukopenia and pancytopenia). These Babesia-specific host data can be separated out, so the record qualifies as a prevalence study that also reports host data.
Prospective infection-risk survey of travelled dogs; no host pathophysiological data.

species: B. rossi and B. vogeli (confirmed, PCR)
rationale: Molecular prevalence survey in dogs and ticks in Nigeria with no host pathophysiological data.
LAMP assay evaluation on DNA samples; no host data.
Serosurvey with no host pathophysiological data.
Review of neurological manifestations of human babesiosis; no dog data.
Human case report of imported B. microti infection.

species: Babesia sp. (confirmed, smear and PCR; species not stated)
rationale: Prospective study of 12 infected dogs against 10 healthy controls reporting CRP, sICAM-1, vWF, fibrinogen and FVIII, relating inflammation to endothelial and haemostatic changes. Already in the review as BG008.
Genome mapping of B. microti isolates; no dog data.
Review of equine piroplasmosis; the host is the horse.

Based on the abstract (PubMed): the neurological signs were attributed to confirmed tick-borne encephalitis, not to Babesia. The babesiosis itself is described only as routine diagnosis and treatment, and the report centres on where the infection was acquired (sequencing), so there is no distinct Babesia syndrome or mechanistic observation.
rescue_reason: Case report of B. canis and TBEV co-infection in a sled dog with neurological signs, plus babesiosis signs in a second dog. The co-infection with neurological disease may be a distinct clinical observation, and the full text may report haematology (low confidence).

rationale: Case report of cerebral babesiosis with ARDS, confirmed at necropsy, with erythrocyte aggregation in lung, liver and brain; a distinct syndrome with histopathology.
Seroprevalence and risk-factor survey with no host pathophysiological data.
Multi-pathogen seroprevalence survey with no host pathophysiological data.

species: none (Angiostrongylus vasorum case; babesiosis ruled out)
rationale: DIC in a dog with A. vasorum infection; babesiosis was excluded, so no Babesia data.

Based on the title and OpenAlex metadata (no abstract; CAB record not open access): a 5-page serosurvey of stray dogs in a regional journal. The title and design point to seroprevalence only, with no indication of host data.
rescue_reason: No abstract. The title is a serosurvey of Babesia in stray dogs, which is probably prevalence-only. The absence of an abstract means host haematology cannot be excluded, so the adjudicator should check the landing page.

rationale: No abstract; the title indicates molecular characterisation of Babesia isolates, which points to parasite genetics with no host data.
Prevalence by age, sex, breed and housing only; no host pathophysiological data.

species: B. gibsoni and B. canis subspecies (review)
rationale: Portuguese-language review of canine babesiosis covering immunological and clinicopathological aspects and differences in pathogenicity and clinical syndromes between species.

Based on the abstract and OpenAlex metadata: a single-author thesis (S.F. Hii, UQ eSpace repository, no journal) on the prevalence of canine vector-borne disease. The thrombocytopaenia association applies to tick-borne infection overall, not to Babesia specifically.
rescue_reason: The abstract reports a thrombocytopaenia association with infection in dogs, including B. vogeli, so host haematology is reported in a prevalence design. The journal field is unknown and the record may be a thesis (not_peer_reviewed), which the adjudicator should confirm.

species: Ehrlichia canis (Babesia only as negative control)
rationale: Abstract-only English text of the E. canis LAMP assay paper (see DOI:10.4067/s0301-732x2013000200012); no Babesia data.
Serological and molecular survey of tick-borne pathogens in Leishmania-seropositive dogs; no host pathophysiological data.

Based on the title and OpenAlex metadata (Shrivastava, Shukla and Swamy, Environment and Ecology 31:342-343; no abstract available): the title explicitly describes a haemato-biochemical profile of naturally infected dogs, which is an eligible clinicopathological case series in a regional journal.
No abstract; the title indicates serodiagnostic and drug-target development, likely a thesis, with no host pathophysiology.

Based on the IPB repository landing page: this is a master's thesis (Maylina, Sajuthi and Esfandiari, IPB University, 2013), not a journal article. It also studies combined Babesia/Haemobartonella infection in 28 dogs, and Babesia-specific data do not appear separable.
IFA serosurvey of 129 dogs in the Brazilian Amazon. It reports exposure frequencies and no host pathophysiological data.

species: B. canis (naturally infected; species method not stated)
rationale: Naturally infected dogs (n=30) versus controls, with serum PON1 activity and HDL measured before and after imidocarb treatment. It tests an antioxidant and lipid peroxidation mechanism.

species: Babesia spp. (unspecified; survey in maned wolves and dogs)
rationale: Based on title only. OpenAlex has no abstract and no DOI, and its CAB Direct landing page returned HTTP 410. The title shows an occurrence survey of several tick-borne pathogens in maned wolves and dogs, and nothing suggests host pathophysiology. Prior rounds excluded maned wolf surveys the same way.
rescue_reason: No abstract. The title describes a pathogen occurrence survey in maned wolves and domestic dogs, which does not rule out haematology or clinical data in infected dogs. Route to adjudicator to check the full text or landing page.

species: B. gibsoni (reported; confirmation method not stated)
rationale: Case report of cerebral babesiosis with seizures and ataxia. It describes a distinct neurological syndrome.
PCR survey of B. canis in questing D. reticulatus ticks in the Czech Republic and Slovakia. It is a vector study and has no dog data.
No abstract. The title shows a comparison of B. canis infection in eastern and western D. reticulatus tick populations, which is a vector study.

species: B. canis (serology and PCR; imported infections)
rationale: Short overview of imported tick-borne infections in German dogs, with prevalence figures. It has no host pathophysiological data.
Prevalence in red foxes, a non-Canis canid, with no dog data.
Molecular survey of pathogens in ticks from Romania. It is a vector study.
Ovine Babesia survey with no dog data.

species: B. vogeli and B. gibsoni (confirmed, PCR); co-infections with E. canis, H. canis, A. platys
rationale: Based on the abstract. It reports thrombocytopenia and anaemia in a case-control PCR study, and only 15% of positive dogs were co-infected, so Babesia-specific haematology may be separable in the full text. The abstract does not show this, so the record goes to full-text review.

species: B. gibsoni and B. canis (microscopy and PCR)
rationale: Compares microscopy with PCR for detection and reports prevalence in suspected cases. It has no host pathophysiological data.

species: B. canis (clinical diagnosis, no molecular confirmation)
rationale: Questionnaire survey of clinical incidence and geographic distribution in France, with no host data.
Detection of Babesia in a bobcat. No dog data.

species: B. canis (culture-derived soluble antigen; dogs not infected)
rationale: Lymphocyte subsets in dogs given culture-derived antigen or a commercial vaccine. The dogs were not infected, so it has no data on host pathophysiology in infected dogs.
Tick pathogen screening in southern Hungary. Babesia was not detected, and there are no host data.

Based on the abstract. The dog host data are good, but the parasite is Rangelia vitalii, a separate piroplasm genus. Rounds 1-3 consistently excluded Rangelia as not_canine_babesia, including mechanistic Rangelia studies.
rescue_reason: Haematology and bone marrow changes in dogs experimentally infected with Rangelia vitalii, with anaemia, neutropenia and erythroid hyperplasia. Rangelia is not a listed canine Babesia, so the adjudicator must decide whether the review admits it. The exclusion as another parasite is contestable because the paper has dog host data.

rationale: Multi-pathogen seroprevalence survey, mainly of Leishmania. No host pathophysiological data.

Based on title and record type. Europe PMC confirms a Letter/Case Report with no abstract. A single imported dog detected in quarantine is a routine diagnostic case with no sign of a distinct syndrome or mechanistic observation.
rescue_reason: Letter on a single quarantined dog infected with B. vogeli. No abstract, and the title does not rule out clinical or haematological findings. Likely a routine case, so the adjudicator should check the full text.

rationale: Based on the abstract. The antibody responses are used as serological markers of exposure in an acaricide-use and infection-status study, not as host immunopathology. The three clinical babesiosis cases are only counted, with no host data.
rescue_reason: Acaricide trial in 30 dogs that also reports humoral immune responses to B. canis and clinical babesiosis in three dogs. The immune response data are host immunity outcomes in dogs exposed to Babesia, even though the design is a prevalence and acaricide study.

species: Not canine (Theileria/B. caballi in ticks from cattle)
rationale: Tick pathogen survey from grazing cattle.
Acaricidal activity of an essential oil against engorged ticks. Vector control only.

Based on the abstract. This is a first-autochthonous-detection report of three dogs, and haematology is only mentioned as part of the diagnostic work-up, with no clinicopathological findings reported. This matches the round 1 exclusion of comparable small detection series.
rescue_reason: First autochthonous canine B. canis canis cases in Latvia (three dogs). The abstract reports a haematological analysis, which is marginal, but the case series is small and the adjudicator should check the clinicopathology.

species: B. bovis and B. bigemina (in vitro)
rationale: Tick cyclophilin A inhibits bovine Babesia in culture. No dog data.

species: B. canis vogeli (confirmed, real-time PCR and RFLP)
rationale: Clinical and haematological profile of 37 PCR-positive dogs compared with negative dogs. It reports normocytic normochromic anaemia, haemoglobinaemia and thrombocytopenia.

species: Babesia (general, in a UK vector-borne disease overview)
rationale: Practice article on vector-borne diseases in UK dogs and cats. Babesiosis is only one of many topics and the article has no pathophysiological focus.
Hepatic oxidative stress in gerbils. It is not a canine study.

species: B. canis (confirmed, PCR/18S sequencing; also in D. reticulatus ticks)
rationale: Based on the abstract. The paper is about outbreak emergence and B. canis DNA in questing ticks. Apart from a crude mortality count (4 of 29 dogs), it reports no host clinical, haematological or outcome data.
rescue_reason: Swiss outbreak of canine babesiosis (29 dogs, 4 deaths) with B. canis DNA in questing ticks. The mortality data are outcome and severity data in infected dogs, which the criteria include. Adjudicator to decide how much host data the full text provides.

rationale: Vector-borne pathogen prevalence in cats. No dog data.

species: B. canis (confirmed by PCR-RFLP in 25 of 70 samples; rest clinically diagnosed, unspecified)
rationale: Based on the abstract. It reports a descriptive clinical phenotype for 836 infected dogs, with frequencies of fever, pallor, changed urine (haemoglobinuria) and splenomegaly. The criteria count descriptive syndrome profiles of infected dogs as evidence even when the study is epidemiological.
Cerebral and haemolytic babesiosis in cats. No dog data.
Human case of babesiosis-associated acute kidney injury. No dog data.
PCR survey of vector-borne pathogens in dogs in Dhaka. No host data.

species: B. gibsoni (blood detection; method not stated in abstract)
rationale: Case with generalized alopecia, skin necrosis and progressive anaemia in babesiosis. Skin histopathology suggests leukocytoclastic vasculitis or ischaemic vasculopathy, which is a distinct vascular syndrome.

Based on the abstract. This is an experimental infection in dogs that compares host responses between attenuated and virulent isolates (parasitaemia, PCV fall, severe anaemia, hyperthermia, antibody titres). That is host-side virulence and immunity data, which the criteria include.
Editorial contents summary of a journal issue, with no abstract or data.

species: Hepatozoon canis; Babesia sp. co-infection in about 4 of 34 dogs (smear only)
rationale: Based on the abstract. The haematology concerns Hepatozoon canis infection. The few Babesia co-infected dogs also carried Ehrlichia, so no Babesia-specific host data can be separated out.
rescue_reason: Clinical and haematological study of dogs with H. canis, with anaemia, leukocytosis and neutrophilia reported. A few dogs had Babesia co-infection. Babesia-specific data are probably not separable, so the adjudicator should decide, but the haematology is reported in infected dogs, which meets the rescue trigger.

rationale: Molecular detection survey in Malaysian dogs. No host data.
Smear-based prevalence study in urban and rural dogs in Ahvaz, with age, sex and season comparisons. No host pathophysiological data.

Based on the abstract. This is a drug-efficacy and resistance study with parasitaemia and relapse endpoints. The ALT increases and hyperphosphatasia are reported as drug side effects, not as disease pathophysiology.
rescue_reason: In vivo atovaquone-proguanil trial in five experimentally infected dogs. It reports biochemistry changes in infected dogs (ALT increases in two dogs and hyperphosphatasia in one), which meets the rescue trigger for host markers in a treatment study.

rationale: Molecular study of B. gibsoni aldolase, actin and erythrocyte invasion mechanics, with no host data from infected dogs.
Cerebral sequestration in calves infected with B. bovis; no dog data.
Survey of ticks and tick-borne pathogens from dogs and cats; no host pathophysiology.

species: Toxoplasma gondii (B. bovis used only as PCR specificity control)
rationale: Toxoplasma real-time PCR assay in mice and pigs; Babesia appears only as a specificity control.
Giemsa search of Rhipicephalus sanguineus hemolymph for B. canis and E. canis; a tick-method study with no host data.
ABCD guideline on feline babesiosis; the host is the cat, not the dog.
