Based on abstract: a single case of diagnosing a piroplasm in a puppy with severe regenerative anaemia. The novel points are geographic (first in Scandinavia) and suspected vertical transmission, not a distinct syndrome or a host-side mechanistic observation, so it stays a routine case report.
rescue_reason: Puppy with severe regenerative anaemia from a piroplasm (Theileria annae, a B. vulpes synonym in scope). The abstract reports a haematology host finding in an infected dog, so it is rescued. The single-case label may still hold at adjudication.

rationale: Case of Ehrlichia infection with clonal T-cell expansion; the dog was Babesia-seronegative.
PCR screening of healthy UK blood donors for infectious agents; no host pathophysiological data.
Postoperative pain after dental implant surgery in patients; unrelated to babesiosis (a false-positive search hit).

species: Babesia sp. (unspecified) with E. canis co-infection
rationale: Based on title and abstract: clinicopathological findings and treatment in dogs that all had babesiosis plus ehrlichiosis. Babesia-specific host data cannot be separated from the co-infection, and it reads as a routine report of diagnosis and treatment.
Characterisation of the BgGARP antigen and an ELISA for serodiagnosis; no host pathophysiology.
Ehrlichiosis treatment and prevention in kennels; all dogs were PCR-negative for Babesia.

species: B. odocoilei / Babesia sp. MO1 (rabbits, deer, ticks)
rationale: Environmental investigation after a human case; wildlife and ticks, no dogs.
Field efficacy trial of an imidacloprid/flumethrin collar against ticks and pathogen transmission; no host pathophysiological data.

species: B. canis (Poland; species per abstract, method not stated)
rationale: Urinary-to-serum creatinine ratio and renal failure index in B. canis-infected dogs versus healthy dogs and by azotaemia, with evidence for acute tubular necrosis.

species: B. canis and B. gibsoni (confirmed, PCR-RFLP and sequencing)
rationale: Species survey of symptomatic dogs in Romania with a breed association; no host pathophysiological data.

species: Babesia spp. (PCR) pooled with Hepatozoon canis
rationale: Based on abstract: a cTnT study of canine monocytic ehrlichiosis. Its only Babesia data come from a 7-dog 'Babesia and/or Hepatozoon' group, so Babesia-specific host data cannot be separated.
rescue_reason: Cardiac troponin and haematology in canine monocytic ehrlichiosis. The 7 Babesia and/or Hepatozoon dogs are pooled, so Babesia-specific data may not separate. Rescued on host markers in infected dogs; the adjudicator should check whether the Babesia subgroup can be separated.

rationale: PCR prevalence of Babesia and Anaplasma in Ixodes ticks from dogs; no host data.
Cloning and characterisation of a B. gibsoni peroxiredoxin with mouse antiserum; no host data from infected dogs.
Hepatozoon diagnosis in dogs and ticks in Venezuela; Babesia is mentioned only in the background.
B. bovis AMA-1 antibody inhibition of erythrocyte invasion in vitro; no dog data.

species: B. gibsoni and B. canis (smear only)
rationale: Hospital-based prevalence of haemoparasites by blood smear in Assam dogs; no host pathophysiological data in the abstract.
Review of human babesiosis in Europe.
B. microti qPCR for ticks and human blood; no dog data.

species: Leishmania infantum (B. canis only as cross-reactivity control)
rationale: Flow cytometry serology for canine leishmaniasis; B. canis sera serve only as cross-reaction controls.
Pathogen survey of a non-Canis canid, with no Babesia detected and no dog data.

species: B. vogeli (confirmed, PCR) with E. canis and A. platys co-infection
rationale: Based on abstract: a routine single case of a triple infection (diagnosis and treatment). The anaemia, thrombocytopenia and biochemical changes cannot be put down to Babesia, and no distinct syndrome is described.
rescue_reason: Dog infected with B. canis vogeli, E. canis and A. platys; the abstract reports anaemia, thrombocytopenia, hypoalbuminaemia, hyperbilirubinaemia and raised ALP and ALT in an infected dog. Rescued on haematology and biochemistry host markers, though co-infection means Babesia-specific effects cannot be separated.

species: B. gibsoni (smear only), co-infection with E. canis
rationale: Based on the PMC full text (PMC3793166): haematology is given only pooled for all 47 ehrlichiosis dogs, and only one dog had E. canis plus B. gibsoni. No Babesia-specific host data can be separated.
rescue_reason: Haematology of 47 ehrlichiosis dogs, about 4 with babesiosis. The abstract reports marked anaemia and neutrophilic leukocytosis and says mixed infection is more severe. Rescued on haematology in infected dogs including Babesia cases; the Babesia subgroup may be separable in the full text.

species: Red fox and fleas (B. microti not detected)
rationale: Molecular survey of pathogens in red foxes and fleas; no dog data.
Consensus statement on serology-positive glomerular disease, mainly Borrelia and Leishmania; Babesia is mentioned only in passing with no Babesia-specific data.
Transcriptome of virulent and attenuated B. bovis strains; cattle parasite, no dog data.

Based on abstract: a Russian narrative review of canine babesiosis whose topics include the clinical forms of the disease and how immunisation affects them. This is marginal because history, vectors and epidemiology take up much of it, but it covers clinical syndromes, as with similar reviews included in rounds 1-3.

Based on abstract (no open-access full text): a prevalence survey that reports PCV by infection status, with co-infected dogs significantly more anaemic. The abstract pools single infections, so full text is needed to see whether PCV or clinical signs are given for the B. vogeli dogs.
Biochemistry of B. bovis thioredoxin reductase; no dog data.

Based on the abstract found in OpenAlex (the AJOL landing page did not load): a smear-based prevalence survey of 150 dogs with age, sex, breed, confinement and tick risk factors. It reports no haematology or other host pathophysiological data.
rescue_reason: Prevalence of B. canis and H. canis in Zaria dogs with no abstract. The title does not rule out host haematology, which such surveys often report. Rescued for a landing-page check.

rationale: Cost-effectiveness model of blood donor screening for human babesiosis.

Haematological changes (anaemia types, thrombocytopenia, leukocyte patterns) correlated with parasitemia in babesiosis, mostly dogs; a clinicopathological profile, though dogs and horses are pooled in the abstract.

Based on abstract: a vaccine protection trial whose endpoints are vaccine-antigen antibody titres and parasitaemia after challenge, with no mechanistic host-response outcomes. This follows the round 1-3 precedent for vaccine trials (for example PMID:29279083).
rescue_reason: DNA and vaccinia prime-boost vaccine in dogs, challenged with B. gibsoni, reporting host antibody responses and parasitaemia. Rescued as an experimental infection with host immune response; the first screener's treatment_efficacy label is doubtful.

rationale: English-language version of the Venezuelan Hepatozoon diagnosis study; Babesia appears only in the background.

species: B. canis / E. canis (mixed or unspecified, serology only)
rationale: Abstract and journal landing page: ECG and cardiac troponin I in 28 anaemic dogs seropositive for E. canis/B. canis, grouped by anaemia severity, with no separation by pathogen. Whether Babesia-specific cardiac data can be pulled out can only be judged from the full text.
Tick survey for pathogens in ticks removed from humans; no dog host data.
Multiplex PCR for Lyme spirochetes, Anaplasma and B. microti in human samples; no dog data.

species: Babesia spp. in wild carnivores; dogs PCR negative
rationale: Molecular prevalence survey in wild carnivores and domestic dogs; dogs were Babesia negative and no host pathophysiology was reported.
Title refers to Babesia-infested buffaloes, not dogs.

Title only. A reference-list entry that I could not resolve in Europe PMC or OpenAlex. The title suggests a haemato-biochemical profile of infected dogs, which would be eligible, so it goes to full-text review.

Duplicate record of PMID:24553975 (Zygner et al., Parasitol Res 2014;113:1499-503), resolved through PubMed. The abstract reports serum TNF-alpha in 11 B. canis-infected dogs, correlated with arterial pressure and renal damage indices (FENa, UCr/SCr, USG): clearly mechanistic host data.

Case of B. gibsoni infection presenting with peritoneal effusion, hypoalbuminaemia and hepatic/renal biochemical changes, an uncommon presentation that bears on vascular permeability and fluid distribution.

Title only: Crossref has no abstract and the publisher PDF linked from the DOI returned 404. The title describes PCR detection of B. canis in dog blood samples in Iran, a molecular detection survey with no sign of host pathophysiological data.
rescue_reason: No abstract is available and the title (PCR detection of B. canis in dog blood, Iran) does not rule out haematology or other host data in infected dogs. Needs full-text check.

rationale: Prevalence of babesiosis and ticks in cattle; no dog data.
Haemoplasma prevalence study by real-time PCR; Babesia is mentioned only as a regional vector-borne parasite.
Europe PMC record: Malaria Journal 2014, 13(Suppl 1):P55, publication type Abstract, with no abstract text. This is a conference poster abstract (Leisewitz et al.), not a peer-reviewed article.
Field incidence study of Cercopithifilaria bainae and co-infection probabilities; no host pathophysiological data.

species: B. canis (seropositive sera used as cross-reactivity panel)
rationale: Serological cross-reactivity of leishmaniasis tests with sera from dogs positive for other pathogens; no host pathophysiology.
Questionnaire survey of babesiosis incidence and distribution in Western Europe; no host data.
Clinicopathological profile of 13 PCR-confirmed dogs with anaemia, thrombocytopenia, monocytosis and lymphocytosis.
Serosurvey of piroplasm antibodies in humans; no dog host data.

species: B. canis (infected dogs, species method not stated in abstract)
rationale: Blood pressure measured in 48 infected dogs; hypotension correlated with creatinine and urea, linking haemodynamics to azotaemia and acute tubular necrosis.

species: B. canis (PCR detection in dogs and Dermacentor ticks)
rationale: Real-time PCR primer development and detection in dog blood and ticks; no host pathophysiological data.
B. ovis in small ruminants and Rhipicephalus bursa ticks; no canine Babesia data.
PCR survey of piroplasms in sheep, dogs and hedgehogs; only two dogs, no host data.

species: B. microti in ticks; not canine
rationale: Co-infection of blacklegged ticks with B. microti and Borrelia; no dog data.

species: B. gibsoni and large Babesia (smear and PCR)
rationale: Prevalence and risk-factor study of canine babesiosis in northwestern India; no host pathophysiology reported.

species: B. divergens in gerbils; not canine
rationale: Splenic pathology and oxidative stress in gerbils infected with B. divergens; no dog data.

species: Babesia not detected (E. canis, H. canis, L. infantum found)
rationale: Molecular survey of co-infecting pathogens in two dogs and ticks; Babesia was not detected and no host data were reported.

Abstract: the study is about vertical transmission, shown by identical 18S sequences in three pups and their dam. The pups' disease is not described beyond 'symptoms', and the dam's splenomegaly is used as evidence of infection, so the report has no usable pathophysiological content.
rescue_reason: Vertical transmission of B. canis in a litter, with clinical babesiosis in three pups and splenomegaly in an infected but asymptomatic dam. Host organ finding and neonatal disease make the stated reason (no usable content) doubtful.

rationale: Tick-borne disease survey in Brazilian Amazon dogs; all samples were Babesia negative and no host pathophysiology was reported.

species: Not applicable (Ixodes ricinus pathogens; not canine Babesia)
rationale: Review of Ixodes ricinus and the pathogens it transmits in urban Europe; no canine babesiosis host data.
Overview of emerging vector-borne diseases with a laboratory sample count in dogs from Serbia; no host pathophysiological data.

species: B. microti antibodies in humans; not canine
rationale: Serosurvey of forestry workers; no dog data.

species: B. microti in a human child; not canine
rationale: Human case of B. microti infection in Canada; no dog data.
Multiplex PCR prevalence survey and veterinarian practice survey in the Philippines; no host pathophysiology.
Clinical and haematological profile of 30 infected dogs (anaemia, thrombocytopenia, icterus, dark urine), which counts as a clinicopathological case series despite the epidemiological framing.

species: B. microti in rats; not canine
rationale: Hepatic histopathology in rats with B. microti; no dog data.

species: Babesia sp. (unspecified; Lithuania, likely B. canis)
rationale: Abstract via OpenAlex: a retrospective haematology and biochemistry series of 300 infected dogs (thrombocytopenia, monocytosis, anaemia, azotaemia and renal failure), which is an eligible clinicopathological profile. The OpenAlex record (Zamokas et al. 2014) points only to the LSMU repository copy of a journal article; the source journal was not confirmed, so check it at extraction.
Twenty-year seasonality and occurrence study of canine babesiosis in Nairobi; no host pathophysiological data.

Landing page (VetMedika J Klin Vet 2014;2(2):32-36): the abstract is one sentence that only defines babesiosis. The hospital case-series title could hold a clinicopathological profile or only occurrence data, which cannot be judged without the full text.

species: B. canis / B. gibsoni (smear only, unspecified)
rationale: Abstract: a drug-combination trial in 18 infected dogs that recorded haemato-biochemical alterations against 6 healthy controls, but no host results are given. Infected-versus-control host data would make it eligible, so it goes to full-text review.
Duplicate record of PMID:25271465 (Portuguese-language OpenAlex copy); co-infection survey with no Babesia detected or host data.
Retrospective proportional-mortality study of hospitalised dogs in Nigeria; babesiosis is one of many causes with no host pathophysiological data.
72 infected dogs vs 25 controls with PCT and NT-pCNP measured, including survivor vs non-survivor comparison. A prognostic inflammatory biomarker study in infected dogs.
Prevalence of Babesia in dogs and ticks in Henan; no host pathophysiological data.
Real-time PCR prevalence of haemoplasmas in dogs; Babesia is only mentioned as a co-vector context.

Based on the abstract, these are two routine diagnosis-and-treatment cases with standard signs and blood counts. The fatal case is put down to hepatic damage and anaemia, but no distinct syndrome or mechanistic observation is described, so the case-report exclusion applies.
rescue_reason: Two dog cases reporting haematology in infected dogs (anaemia, leucocytosis, low haemoglobin, erythrocyte and platelet counts) and a fatal case attributed to hepatic damage and anaemia. The exclusion as a routine case report is borderline, so the adjudicator should decide whether it qualifies as a clinicopathological case with host markers.

rationale: 30 infected dogs vs 10 controls with thrombomodulin, HMGB-1, ICAM-1, suPAR and AT III measured at admission and day 6, linking coagulation, endothelial activation and inflammation.

species: Babesia sp. in mice (no dog data)
rationale: Experimental babesiosis in mice with stomach histology; no dog data.
Serial PGE2, TxB2, LTB4 and lipid profile in infected dogs with SIRS and MODS compared with healthy dogs. Mechanistic and severity-related host data.

species: B. canis (confirmed, PCR and sequencing); Canis lupus (grey wolf)
rationale: Fatal acute babesiosis in two grey wolves (Canis lupus counts as canine evidence), with necropsy findings of severe jaundice, hepatosplenomegaly, pale kidneys and petechiae. Pathological observations, not a routine treatment case.

Based on the abstract, this is a PCR and serology survey of sled dogs. The only host-level findings are counts of clinical versus asymptomatic dogs and a TBEV-serology risk link, with no haematological, biochemical or organ data for the Babesia-infected dogs.
rescue_reason: Sled dog survey that reports clinical babesiosis in 4 dogs and an association between TBEV seropositivity and prior B. canis infection. The host-level serological association is weak, so the adjudicator should check the full text for haematology or other host markers.

species: B. canis and B. gibsoni (serology, microscopy)
rationale: Seroprevalence survey of vector-borne parasites in dogs in Assam; no host pathophysiological data.
Tick-based surveillance of human babesiosis; no dog data.
Molecular co-infection survey in clinically healthy Dirofilaria-positive dogs; no host pathophysiological data.
Babesiosis case in a macaque; no dog data.
Review of parasitic zoonoses in Egypt; babesiosis is mentioned only as a human zoonosis, with no canine pathophysiology.

species: Wild ungulates and carnivores (T. annae in foxes; wolves negative)
rationale: Molecular survey of piroplasms in wildlife (mostly deer, boar and fox); no dog data and no host pathophysiology.

Experimental challenge in immunised vs control dogs reports host responses: humoral antibody titres, PCV fall, severe anaemia and hyperthermia in controls. Only two dogs per group, so weak, but host-side immune and haematological data are present.

species: B. canis (confirmed, PCR in ticks; dogs clinical diagnosis)
rationale: Based on the abstract, this is a 13-year study of case occurrence, recurrence, tick abundance and prevention in one kennel. The splenomegaly and splenic rupture leading to splenectomy is a single passing mention with no host pathophysiological data.
rescue_reason: Thirteen-year sled dog kennel study that reports recurrent babesiosis in individual dogs and a splenectomy after splenomegaly and spleen rupture in an infected dog. That is a severe host complication, which the passing-mention exclusion treats too lightly, so it is rescued for adjudication.

rationale: Serum TNF-alpha correlated with arterial pressure and renal damage indices (FENa, UCr/SCr, RFI, USG, UPC) in 11 infected dogs. Mechanistic link between cytokine, hypotension and renal failure.

species: B. gibsoni, B. bovis (in vitro); B. microti (mice)
rationale: IMPDH inhibitors tested on recombinant enzyme, in vitro cultures and a mouse model; drug-target work with no canine host data.
Mitochondrial genome of a buffalo Babesia; no dog data.

Based on the abstract on the Veterinary World landing page, reached via the DOI: an experimental infection of 5 dogs against 5 uninfected controls. It reports the clinical course (haemoglobinuria, respiratory distress, oedema, one death) and biochemistry, with ALP and ALT higher and glucose and creatinine lower than in controls, so it qualifies as an experimental infection that reports host responses.
Tick prevalence and seasonal abundance on dogs and the role of R. sanguineus as vector. The title points to a vector study with no host pathophysiology.

species: B. canis (PCR in D. reticulatus ticks)
rationale: Pathogen prevalence in questing ticks; no dog data.

species: B. canis, B. vogeli, B. rossi, B. gibsoni (PCR)
rationale: Optimisation and comparison of a semi-nested PCR for diagnosis; no host pathophysiological data.
Oxidative stress and DNA damage in goats; no dog data.
PCR survey of vector-borne pathogens in dogs in Costa Rica; no host pathophysiological data.
In vitro doxycycline sensitivity of cultured B. gibsoni by real-time PCR; no host data.

Based on the one-sentence OpenAlex abstract and title only, because the journal landing page returned 404. The paper describes how piroplasmosis presents in dogs of different ages, which suggests clinical or clinicopathological profiles, but whether host data are reported cannot be judged without the full text.

Based on the abstract, the pathogen is Rangelia vitalii, which rounds 1-3 consistently excluded as outside the Babesia scope. The study is mainly about a wild Cerdocyon thous, and the single inoculated dog is reported only as developing clinical rangeliosis, with no host data.
rescue_reason: Rangelia vitalii in a wild crab-eating fox, with a dog inoculated with infected blood that developed clinical rangeliosis. Dog data are present, which takes the record out of the non-Canis exclusion, so the adjudicator should check the dog's clinical and haematological data.

rationale: PCR prevalence survey of vector-borne pathogens in cats; no dog data.
Molecular survey of tick-borne pathogens and ticks in dogs in Nigeria, including BrEMA1 screening (parasite genotype). No host pathophysiological data.
Molecular confirmation of a human B. microti case with a new beta-tubulin PCR; no canine host data.
qPCR survey of vector-borne agents in apparently healthy dogs in Nicaragua; no host pathophysiological data.

species: Babesia (serology and PCR panel; not separated)
rationale: Comparison of serological and molecular panels for canine vector-borne diseases; no Babesia-specific host pathophysiology.
Human case report of severe babesiosis in Spain; no abstract and no dog data.

species: Not tested (Babesia not among assayed pathogens)
rationale: Seroprevalence of Anaplasma, Borrelia, Ehrlichia and Dirofilaria in healthy Hungarian dogs; no Babesia data and no host pathophysiology.
Pyrosequencing assay for differential detection of canine haemopathogens; no host data.
Piroplasm diversity in ticks from several US states; no dog host data.

species: T. annae/B. vulpes in red foxes
rationale: Molecular survey of piroplasms in red foxes and their ticks; non-Canis canid and no dog data.
Short conference-proceedings overview of tick-borne disease emergence, with hepatozoonosis and canine babesiosis in Mendoza. It reports no host pathophysiological data.
Molecular survey of pathogens in ticks from dogs, cats and vegetation. It reports no host data from infected dogs.
Hepatic CYP2D expression in B. microti-infected mice. There are no dog data.
Human case report of babesiosis presenting with ARDS. There are no dog data.
Heparin binding of a Theileria orientalis surface protein, tested on bovine cells. It concerns neither canine Babesia nor infected dogs.

species: B. bigemina, B. bovis, B. divergens (not canine)
rationale: Comparative genomics of variant antigen genes in bovine Babesia species. It reports no host data and no dog data.

species: B. canis canis (confirmed by the authors; naturally infected dogs)
rationale: Serum proteomics in 25 naturally infected dogs against healthy controls, with serial samples. It identifies acute-phase, complement, coagulation and haemolysis-related proteins as pathogenic mechanisms.
Oxidative DNA damage (8-OHdG), nitric oxide and total antioxidant capacity in infected dogs against controls. This is a host oxidative stress study.
Molecular survey of Theileria in cervids. There are no dog data.

species: Ehrlichia canis survey; Babesia status only as a covariate
rationale: Serological and PCR survey of E. canis in Japanese dogs. It reports no Babesia host pathophysiology.
Pathogen detection in ticks from domestic animals in central China. There are no host data from infected dogs.
Renal function profile in 20 dogs with babesiosis (urea, creatinine, electrolytes, urine specific gravity). It describes the renal syndrome in infected dogs.
Infection of questing Dermacentor reticulatus ticks in the Chernobyl exclusion zone. It reports no dog data.
PCR survey of dogs in Guangxi with phylogeny. It reports no host pathophysiological data.

From the abstract: ultrasonographic liver and spleen changes in 101 dogs with tick-borne diseases. The findings seem to be listed per disease, babesiosis among them, but the abstract does not show whether Babesia-specific data can be separated, so full-text review is needed.
Molecular detection of arthropod-borne agents in free-roaming cats. There are no dog data.

From the abstract: a review of canine rangeliosis. Rangelia is a separate piroplasm genus, and rounds 1-3 consistently excluded Rangelia records as not_canine_babesia even when they had mechanistic content.
Clinicopathological profile of six dogs with babesiosis: anaemia, thrombocytopenia, hypoalbuminaemia, and raised ALT, creatinine and BUN. Such profiles count as descriptive syndrome evidence.
Anti-erythrocyte autoantibodies in B. rodhaini-infected mice. There are no dog data.

From the abstract and MeSH: a Malarone/doxycycline trial in 8 dogs with parasitaemia and relapse endpoints. The anaemia and biochemistry are treatment-response measures, not a host-mechanism focus, which matches how rounds 1-3 handled drug trials.
rescue_reason: Malarone trial in dogs naturally infected with B. gibsoni. The abstract reports anaemia improvement, and the MeSH terms list ALT, ALP, bilirubin, BUN, creatinine, blood cell count and globulins, so host haematology and biochemistry are likely reported in infected dogs. Scoring against the stated treatment-only reason is wrong (ERY/MET).

rationale: Nationwide molecular survey of Haemaphysalis longicornis for B. gibsoni. It is a vector study with no host data.

From the abstract: an acaricide trial on blocking transmission. Hyperthermia in the control dogs served only as an infection endpoint and no host-response data are reported, which matches earlier acaricide-trial exclusions.
rescue_reason: Afoxolaner transmission trial in dogs. Infected control dogs had hyperthermia and clinical babesiosis confirmed, which is a host clinical and inflammatory response. The primary endpoints are transmission, so the adjudicator should judge this borderline (vector_tick/treatment).

species: Rangelia vitalii (confirmed, PCR-RFLP/18S sequencing); not Babesia
rationale: From the abstract: a first-report case of Rangelia vitalii, a non-Babesia piroplasm, with routine haematology and a focus on molecular identification. This matches the Rangelia scope decision from rounds 1-3.
rescue_reason: Dog with Rangelia vitalii (canine piroplasm, Babesia sensu stricto clade). The case reports regenerative anaemia, epistaxis and bone marrow findings in an infected dog, so dog host data are present. The stated not_canine_babesia reason is wrong for this dog case. The routine first-report nature may lead the adjudicator to other_out_of_scope.

species: B. canis, B. venatorum in ticks
rationale: Tick distribution and Rickettsia and Babesia prevalence in questing ticks in Slovakia. There are no host data.

species: B. venatorum in ticks from humans
rationale: Ticks removed from humans in Italy and the pathogens they carry. There are no dog data.
Oxidative stress in ovine babesiosis. It is a mechanistic study, but the host is sheep and there are no dog data.

species: Hepatozoon in wild canids; putative Babesia in foxes
rationale: Hepatozoon prevalence in North African wild canids and rodents. The only Babesia detections are in foxes, with no dog data.

species: Babesia sp. (naturally infected dogs; species not stated in the abstract)
rationale: PON1 activity, HDL and CRP in 29 dogs with babesiosis against 15 controls, sampled at admission and after treatment. It reports lipid peroxidation and the acute-phase response (already BG015, screened as a new record).

species: None (Babesia PCR negative; E. canis seropositive in one dog)
rationale: Cold agglutinin activity in two dogs. Babesia PCR was negative, so there is no Babesia infection and no Babesia host data.

species: Babesia sp. (suspected, smear/SNAP); mixed with Ehrlichia/Hepatozoon/Anaplasma
rationale: From the reconstructed abstract: haemato-biochemical and oxidative stress indices in dogs with concomitant tick-borne infections, which is relevant content. The data are given for the mixed-infection group, and the full text is needed to see whether Babesia-containing subgroups can be separated.
Human case report of babesiosis in pregnancy. There are no dog data.

species: B. rossi and others in ticks from humans
rationale: Tick-borne pathogens in ticks removed from humans in Turkey. There are no dog data.
Review of parasite molecules for diagnosis, vaccine and drug development. It is not about host pathophysiology.

species: B. gibsoni Asian genotype (PCR, sequenced); unnamed Babesia sp.
rationale: Genetic characterisation and phylogeny of small canine Babesia from India. It reports no host data.
Cost-effectiveness model of donor screening for B. microti. It concerns humans, not dogs.

Serum urea-to-creatinine ratio in 48 infected dogs, compared between azotaemic and non-azotaemic dogs and correlated with arterial blood pressure. It addresses the mechanism of azotaemia and hypotension.

species: Theileria sp. and T. equi (confirmed, PCR-RLB); Babesia PCR-negative
rationale: From the abstract: the dogs had Theileria sp. and T. equi, not T. annae/B. vulpes, and were Babesia PCR-negative. Dog host data do not bring other parasites into scope, and earlier rounds excluded similar records.
rescue_reason: Six dogs with Theileria infection and Babesia PCR negative. The dogs have host haematology (thrombocytopenia, anaemia, bleeding, myelofibrosis) and a suspected immune-mediated syndrome, so dog host data are present. The not_canine_babesia code is correct for Babesia, but the rescue rule applies to other parasites with dog data. The adjudicator should decide the Theileria scope.

species: None (Babesia used only for PCR cross-reaction testing)
rationale: Prevalence survey of zoonotic pathogens in stray dogs in Taiwan. Babesia is mentioned only for primer specificity, and there are no host data.
Prevalence of tick-borne pathogens in dogs in Thailand, with a treatment and parasite-elimination component. It reports no host pathophysiological data.
Overview of zoonotic tick-borne pathogens in southern Africa. There are no canine Babesia host data.
Development and evaluation of recombinant BgSA1 serodiagnostic ELISAs. It reports no host pathophysiology.

species: Babesia spp. (PCR screen; none reported in Ghana dogs)
rationale: Molecular survey of vector-borne pathogens in Ghanaian dogs with no host pathophysiological data.
Detection and 18S genotyping of B. canis in Lithuanian dogs; no host haematology, biochemistry or other pathophysiological data.

species: Leishmania infantum; babesiosis sera only as cross-reactivity controls
rationale: Evaluation of a Leishmania serological assay. Babesia appears only as a cross-reacting group and there are no host pathophysiology data.

Based on the abstract: a drug efficacy and safety study. The BUN/creatinine rise was AmB nephrotoxicity at 1 mg/kg and the methaemoglobin change was drug-induced in normal erythrocytes in vitro, so neither is host pathophysiology of the infection; the rescue is declined.
rescue_reason: Amphotericin B study with in vivo data in B. gibsoni-infected dogs. BUN and creatinine were abnormally elevated after 1 mg/kg, which is an organ-function host marker in infected dogs inside a treatment study. The erythrocyte methaemoglobin and oxidative-damage findings are also mechanistic.

species: B. canis canis (confirmed per authors; method not stated in abstract)
rationale: Based on the abstract: a diagnostic MALDI-TOF study. It reports a 51-52 kDa serum protein fraction found only in infected dogs, but the abstract does not say whether this is a host protein (e.g. an acute-phase reactant) or a parasite antigen. Sent to full text to check for host-proteome data.
rescue_reason: MALDI-TOF study comparing infected and healthy dogs. A 51-52 kDa serum protein present in all infected dogs is proposed as a disease marker, which is a host biomarker finding in infected dogs inside a diagnostic study. Its identity is not established, but the record is not ruled out.

rationale: Porcine babesiosis PCR and epidemiology; no dog data.
Serological surveillance of US dogs for multiple vector-borne pathogens; no host pathophysiological data.

Based on title and venue only (no abstract available): a conference proceedings item (Korean Society of Veterinary Clinics academic conference proceedings) on the clinical efficacy of atovaquone/proguanil, so it is both a conference abstract and a treatment-efficacy topic.
Histology of the mouse stomach in experimental babesiosis; no dog data.
Macrophage depletion in murine B. microti infection; no dog data.
Human apheresis review that mentions babesiosis only in passing; no dog data.
Human case reports of Evans syndrome with babesiosis; no dog data.

species: B. canis (natural infection; confirmation method not stated in abstract)
rationale: Serum aldosterone, blood pressure and azotaemia in 14 infected dogs versus 10 healthy dogs. It gives endocrine and haemodynamic evidence on hyperaldosteronism and renal failure.

species: B. leo, B. vogeli in felids
rationale: Molecular survey of tick-borne pathogens in captive wild felids; no dog data.
Acaricide speed-of-kill trial against ticks; no Babesia data.
General haematology review of red cells as infection targets; no dog data.
Molecular survey of foxes; no dog data.

species: B. gibsoni (in vitro only), plus other Babesia and B. microti in mice
rationale: In vitro and mouse growth-inhibition study of trichostatin A; no infected-dog host data.
Distribution survey of B. gibsoni in Japanese hunting dogs by microscopy and PCR; no host pathophysiological data.
Tick species survey on dogs in Romania; Babesia is mentioned only as a risk.

species: B. canis canis, B. vogeli, B. gibsoni (confirmed, real-time PCR and sequencing)
rationale: Molecular prevalence and isolate characterisation in Turkish dogs; no host pathophysiological data.

Based on the title only; the OpenAlex record and KrishiKosh landing page give no abstract or journal. The title describes a routine single-pup clinical case report with no sign of a distinct syndrome or mechanistic observation.

Based on the abstract and PMC full text (PMC4261574): none of the 83 dogs had a B. vogeli single infection. The 5 B. vogeli dogs were all co-infected and were pooled into a co-infection group, so Babesia-specific host data cannot be separated out.
Pathogen screening of ticks collected from dogs; no host data.
Letter on serum ferritin in human babesiosis; no dog data.
Cortisol, insulin and glucose in infected dogs before and after treatment, compared with healthy dogs and between survivors and non-survivors. It gives endocrine response and prognostic evidence.
Arterial blood pressure in 30 infected dogs and 20 healthy dogs, with hypotension in complicated cases and a link to outcome. It gives haemodynamic and severity evidence.

species: B. canis (confirmed per authors; method not stated)
rationale: Based on the Hrčak landing page abstract (Vet Arhiv 84(6):575-589, 2014): 72 dogs with babesiosis vs 25 controls. PCT differed between infected and healthy dogs, and NT-proCNP differed between survivors and non-survivors, so these are host inflammatory and prognostic markers.
Description of a new rodent Babesia species; no dog data.

species: T. equi and B. caballi in horses and donkeys
rationale: Equine piroplasm survey. One dog carried T. equi and there are no host pathophysiological data.
In vitro drug sensitivity study of artemisinin derivatives; no host data.
Vector-borne pathogen survey in arctic foxes; no dog data.

Based on the abstract: a general review of cardiac troponins in dogs. Babesiosis appears only in a list of conditions with raised troponin, so the review's subject is not canine babesiosis; the rescue is declined.
rescue_reason: Review of cardiac troponins in dogs. The abstract states that babesiosis raises troponin levels in dogs, which is a cardiac host-marker claim in infected dogs. It is only a passing mention, so the yield is low and the adjudicator may decline it.

rationale: Hospital prevalence of protozoan diseases in dogs; no host pathophysiological data.
Editorial and tribute on interferon research; unrelated to canine babesiosis.

species: B. rossi and B. gibsoni, single and mixed (confirmed, molecular)
rationale: Resolved via PubMed to PMID:26682062 (Nalubamba et al., J Parasitol Res 2015, first pub 2015-11-22, in window); based on the abstract. A clinicopathological profile of 363 infected dogs (anaemia in 96.4%, nucleated erythrocytes) related to Babesia species.

Resolved via PubMed to PMID:30155438 (Köster, Lobetti, Kelly, Vet Med (Auckl) 2015;6:119-128, first pub 2015-04-10, in window); based on the abstract. A narrative review of complicated canine babesiosis, immune-mediated anaemia, inflammatory complications and prognostic biomarkers.

Duplicate record of PMID:25347616 (Hyperaldosteronism and its association with hypotension and azotaemia in canine babesiosis, Vet Q 2014/2015). The reference-list title is a mis-citation, so the record gets the same include decision; based on title match with the abstract of the canonical record.

Based on the title only; PubMed, Europe PMC and Crossref searches did not resolve it to a published record. The title describes oxidative-stress host data in naturally infected dogs, which would be eligible, but the venue, peer-review status and date cannot be confirmed.
Reference-list entry whose title covers B. microti transmission from Ixodes persulcatus to humans; no dog data.
Seroprevalence in clinically healthy dogs; no abstract, and the title shows no host pathophysiology.

species: B. canis (suspected, smear only) with E. canis co-infection
rationale: Based on the abstract. This is a routine single case of Ehrlichia/Babesia co-infection, diagnosed by smear and cured with imidocarb and doxycycline. The haemorrhagic signs and red urine cannot be attributed to Babesia rather than Ehrlichia, and no mechanistic observation or distinct Babesia syndrome is described.
rescue_reason: Named syndrome (Lahore canine fever) in a dog with haemorrhagic signs (gum streaks, palatal ecchymosis) and red urine, which suggests haemoglobinuria. The routine-case exclusion looks wrong; mixed Ehrlichia/Babesia needs adjudicator check.

species: B. canis (serology only, exposure) with multiple co-exposures
rationale: Based on the abstract. This is a seroprevalence survey in which seroreactivity shows exposure, not active infection. The only significant laboratory differences are tied to B. burgdorferi, E. canis and R. conorii, not B. canis, so no Babesia-specific host data can be separated out.
rescue_reason: Compares haematological and biochemical parameters (RBC, albumin, AST) and clinical signs between seropositive and seronegative dogs, including B. canis seroreactivity. Host markers in infected dogs inside a prevalence study, so the exclusion is not safe.

species: B. microti (confirmed, PCR and serology) in one dog co-infected with B. canis, A. phagocytophilum and R. conorii
rationale: Based on the full-text PDF from the landing page (published 16 Oct 2015). This prevalence survey of 89 dogs found one positive dog, co-infected with other pathogens, with nonspecific signs and a normal blood count, so there are no separable Babesia-specific host pathophysiological data.
rescue_reason: No abstract. The title (serological and molecular investigation of B. microti in dogs) does not rule out host clinical or haematological data. Adjudicator to check the landing page.

rationale: Tick infestation and tick-borne disease prevalence in Indonesian dogs; no host pathophysiological data.

species: B. vogeli (confirmed, PCR in 5 of 17 smear-positive dogs)
rationale: Based on the abstract and full-text PDF. This prevalence and risk-factor study gives only a descriptive list of clinical signs, plus gross necropsy findings and deaths in three puppies, with no haematology, biochemistry or mechanistic data. The host-side content is incidental to the prevalence aim.
rescue_reason: Abstract reports clinical phenotype of infected dogs (pyrexia, anorexia, weight loss, pale mucosa) and age-related severity (puppies). This is severity-relevant host data, though no haematology is given. Adjudicator to check the full text.

rationale: Retrospective disease incidence survey of clinic records; babesiosis is one of 31 conditions and no host data are reported.

species: Not applicable (B. canis transmission prevention mentioned)
rationale: Editorial on a fipronil/permethrin ectoparasiticide collection; acaricide and vector control with no host data.

species: B. canis (confirmed, diagnosis in infected dogs)
rationale: Flow cytometry of lymphocyte subsets (CD3, CD4, CD8, CD21) in infected dogs versus healthy controls, before and after imidocarb; reports host immune responses.
Serological co-infection and cross-reaction study in urban dogs; no host pathophysiological data.
Serological and molecular survey with no host pathophysiological data.
Mainly a survey, but it uses haemograms from infected dogs and reports that B. vogeli PCR positivity was associated with thrombocytopenia, which is Babesia-specific host data.
Experimental B. bovis infection of deer and cattle; no dog data.
Human Medicare claims epidemiology; no dog data.
Molecular prevalence survey in stray dogs; no host pathophysiological data.
18S rRNA genotyping of B. canis from subclinical dogs; parasite genetics with no host data.
Review of human babesiosis diagnosis and management; no dog data.
General overview of Babesia morphology, epidemiology and phylogeny in domestic animals; no canine host pathophysiology.

species: B. rossi and B. gibsoni (single and mixed; confirmed)
rationale: Clinicopathological case series of 363 infected dogs reporting haematology (anaemia in 96%, nucleated erythrocytes) in relation to species; a clinicopathological profile.
Human case report; no dog data.
Human Borrelia/Babesia coinfection review; no dog data.
Development of a multiplex PCR evaluated on tick DNA; no host data.
Theileria survey in Caribbean livestock; no dog data.
Review of clinical complications, biomarkers and prognosis in canine babesiosis, including immune-mediated anaemia and the inflammatory response.
Prevalence by blood smear in febrile dogs; no host pathophysiological data.

Title and OpenAlex metadata only, since no abstract could be found and the University of Nairobi repository was unreachable. It is a 3-page prevalence study of clinical babesiosis and ehrlichiosis (Int J Vet Sci 4(2):60-62), and nothing in the record suggests Babesia-specific host pathophysiological data.
rescue_reason: No abstract. The title (prevalence of clinical canine babesiosis and ehrlichiosis in Nairobi) does not rule out host clinical or haematological data. Adjudicator to check the landing page.

rationale: Based on the abstract (Russian). This acaricide trial measures tick counts and prevention of B. canis transmission. Temperature, PCR and smears were used only to detect infection, after which infected dogs were treated and replaced, so no host-response outcomes are reported.
rescue_reason: Russian-language fluralaner trial in which infected dogs were monitored for rectal temperature, clinical babesiosis signs and smears. Results are not shown in the abstract, so host data cannot be ruled out. Adjudicator to check the full text.

species: B. canis (spontaneous infection; method not stated)
rationale: Clinical signs and erythrocyte morphological changes in naturally infected dogs (haemoglobinuria, anuria, nervous signs, inclusions); a clinical and haematological profile.
Incidence by sex and season in Kolkata dogs; no host pathophysiological data.
Morphological identification of Rhipicephalus sanguineus on dogs; vector study with no host data.
Expression and epitope mapping of the BgTRAP antigen; parasite antigen work with no host data.

species: B. gibsoni (confirmed by case diagnosis; method not stated)
rationale: Case of immune-mediated haemolytic anaemia secondary to B. gibsoni, a distinct immune-mediated syndrome, with discussion of diagnosis, treatment and prognosis.

Title and OpenAlex metadata only; no abstract could be found (the CAB Direct page has been removed). A case of babesiosis that needed haemodialysis suggests a severe acute kidney injury complication, which may be a distinct renal syndrome, so the full text is needed.

species: B. canis (suspected, smear only) with Dipylidium caninum
rationale: Based on the abstract. This is a routine single case with the typical presentation (haemolytic anaemia, haemoglobinaemia, leukocytosis) and treatment. It describes no distinct syndrome or mechanistic observation, and its focus is on occurrence and zoonotic advice.
rescue_reason: Single case of dipylidiasis and babesiosis reporting haematology: leukocytosis, lymphocytosis, reduced RBC from haemolytic anaemia, and haemoglobinaemia. This is a haemolysis observation in an infected dog, so the routine-case exclusion looks wrong.

species: Livestock Babesia (B. bigemina, B. bovis, others)
rationale: Overview of livestock babesiosis in Karnataka; dogs are only mentioned in passing.
Comparison of PCR protocols for genotyping archival smears and tissue imprints; methodological, with only merozoite morphology and no host pathophysiology.
Necropsy and histology of cardiac lesions in 20 dogs that died of complicated B. canis infection, including haemorrhage, necrosis, sludging and microthrombi.

species: B. canis (confirmed, PCR/sequencing, 3 dogs); Theileria sp. in 1 dog; co-infections
rationale: Based on the abstract and OpenAlex metadata. The landing page is a J Comp Pathol meeting-abstract PDF, and the structured template with 'Discussion (and/or Conclusions)' is a conference abstract format. The content is mainly pathogen genotyping in archival tissues, with no separable Babesia-specific host pathology.

Title and OpenAlex metadata only; there is no abstract and the LSMU repository PDF was unreachable. The title ('Prevalence/distribution of B. canis infection in dogs in Alytus county') shows a single-author distribution survey, possibly a student work, with nothing suggesting host pathophysiological data.
rescue_reason: No abstract. The title (distribution of B. canis infection in dogs in Alytus county) does not rule out host data. Likely a prevalence survey, so the adjudicator should confirm from the landing page.

rationale: Archaeological and historical argument about disease constraining dog spread in Africa; canine babesiosis is discussed as a threat without host pathophysiological data.

species: Babesia spp. (PCR, unspecified), mixed with E. canis and others
rationale: Incidence and diagnostic-probability study of canine monocytic ehrlichiosis in southern Europe. Babesia is only one of several co-detected pathogens and no Babesia-specific host data are given.
Review of vector ecology of equine piroplasmosis. No dog data.

Based on the title and the Semantic Scholar summary (the Springer landing page redirected to an access flow and the abstract is withheld): a dog with recurrent skin lesions, fever and weight loss linked to babesiosis on blood smear. This is an atypical cutaneous syndrome (likely vascular or ischaemic), so it qualifies as a distinct-syndrome case report; published 2015-01, in window.
Tests a fipronil-permethrin product for blocking tick transmission of B. canis. Endpoint is seroconversion and PCR positivity, with no host pathophysiology.
Molecular detection and genetic diversity of B. gibsoni in stray dogs in Bangladesh. No host clinicopathological data.

species: Not applicable (D. reticulatus ticks on dogs)
rationale: Acaricide repellency and efficacy against D. reticulatus. No Babesia infection data in dogs.

species: B. cf. microti in red foxes (PCR)
rationale: PCR survey of red foxes. Non-Canis canid and no dog data.

species: B. canis (B. c. vogeli and B. c. canis, PCR)
rationale: Molecular prevalence survey of vector-borne pathogens in asymptomatic hunting dogs. No host pathophysiological data.
Clinical review of human tick-borne infections. No dog data.

species: B. bigemina / B. bovis in deer
rationale: Babesia detection in fallow and axis deer. No dog data.

Based on the abstract summary from Semantic Scholar (the AJOL page returned no content): a household prevalence survey (9/101 infected) with risk factors such as age, sex, breed, management and ticks. No host haematology or pathophysiology is reported.

species: B. canis / B. cf. microti in red foxes (PCR)
rationale: Molecular survey of vector-borne pathogens in red foxes. No dog data.
PCR prevalence and risk-factor study of Babesia in dogs in Cuiaba, Brazil. No host pathophysiology.

species: Not applicable (ticks on dogs and cats)
rationale: Owner-based tick survey in Switzerland. Tick vector study with no Babesia host data.

species: B. gibsoni and B. canis (species mix, smear or unspecified)
rationale: Eight-year incidence trends of canine babesiosis in Chennai with age, sex and breed factors. No pathophysiological data in the abstract.
Tick distribution modelling related to equine piroplasmosis. No dog Babesia data.
Recombinant antigen for diagnosis of ovine babesiosis. No dog data.

species: B. gibsoni (in vitro) and Haemaphysalis longicornis
rationale: Tick innate immune protein with in vitro growth inhibition of B. gibsoni. Tick and parasite study with no dog host data.

species: B. gibsoni (confirmed, LAMP and nested PCR)
rationale: Development of a LAMP assay for B. gibsoni. No host pathophysiology.

species: B. canis canis (naturally infected; method not stated in abstract)
rationale: Malondialdehyde as a lipid peroxidation marker in 30 infected dogs against healthy controls. Levels are higher in complicated disease and MODS and correlate with outcome.

species: B. gibsoni (confirmed per abstract, method not stated); B. canis (1 dog)
rationale: Based on the abstract: a retrospective series of anaemic dogs graded by haematocrit, in which B. gibsoni caused 36 of the 43 infectious very severe anaemia cases. This gives Babesia-specific data on anaemia severity in infected dogs, so I agree with the second screener's rescue.
rescue_reason: Taiwan anaemia causes in dogs: B. gibsoni was the pathogen in 36 of 43 infectious-disease very severe anaemia cases, so this is Babesia-specific anaemia severity data in infected dogs. The first-screener exclusion (prevalence) is wrong. Category ERY, secondary SEV.

species: B. canis vogeli (naturally infected, uncomplicated cases)
rationale: Serum cystatin-C, urea and creatinine in 16 infected dogs against E. canis-infected dogs and healthy controls. Cystatin-C is raised in babesiosis, indicating renal injury.

Based on the abstract (no open full text in Europe PMC): a proportion and risk-factor survey of tick-borne pathogens. The thrombocytopenia association is pooled across all pathogens, and the abstract gives no B. vogeli-specific host data.
rescue_reason: Northern Australia tick-borne pathogen study with thrombocytopenia reported as a risk association for infection with CTBD pathogens, which include B. vogeli (5.0%). Babesia-specific data may not be separable from the pooled result, so the adjudicator should check the full text. Category COA.

species: B. canis vogeli (PCR) and Hepatozoon canis
rationale: Development of a qFRET PCR assay with melting curve analysis. No host pathophysiology.
Historical and biographical note on Victor Babes. No data.
Human case report of fatal babesiosis and Lyme coinfection. No dog data.
B. ovis prevalence in small ruminants. Farm dogs were examined only for ticks.
Molecular survey of tick-borne pathogens in asymptomatic dogs in Turkey. No host pathophysiology.
qPCR against blood smear in human B. microti infection. No dog data.
Molecular detection of Rangelia vitalii in two dogs. A different piroplasm, not Babesia.

species: Filarioids; B. vogeli only as co-infection
rationale: Evaluation of filarioid detection methods in Costa Rica. Babesia appears only as a co-infection, with no Babesia host data.
PCR prevalence survey of vector-borne pathogens in southern Portugal. No dogs were Babesia positive and there are no host data.
Phylogenetic reclassification of T. annae as Babesia vulpes. No new host data.

Based on the abstract: a Rickettsia febrile-illness case-control study in which Babesia appears only as a PCR detection rate (about 4 dogs, all febrile). It has no Babesia-specific clinicopathological or mechanistic data, and fever alone in a handful of co-detected dogs does not meet the host-pathophysiology criterion.
rescue_reason: Rickettsia febrile illness study in which Babesia spp. PCR positives (4.0%) were found only in febrile dogs, with B. vogeli sequences. This is Babesia-specific fever association in infected dogs, and the first-screener exclusion overlooked it. Category INF, secondary SEV.

species: B. vulpes / Theileria annae (confirmed, PCR and sequencing)
rationale: Clinical series of 75 PCR-confirmed dogs. Blood counts show severe regenerative anaemia and thrombocytopenia, a clinicopathological profile of infected dogs.

species: B. canis in D. reticulatus ticks (PCR and RLB)
rationale: Surveillance of D. reticulatus ticks infected with B. canis and B. caballi. Tick study with no dog host data.

species: Anaplasma platys / Ehrlichia canis; B. vogeli only as a specificity control
rationale: qPCR development and ocular lesions in A. platys and E. canis infection. Babesia appears only as an analytical specificity control.
Clinical pathology of equine piroplasmosis in donkeys. No dog data.

species: Rangelia vitalii (PCR positive; Babesia spp. PCR negative)
rationale: Single case report of rangeliosis in a dog. The agent is Rangelia vitalii, and PCR was negative for Babesia spp.

species: B. canis vogeli (IFA, smear, tick PCR)
rationale: Seroprevalence, tick infestation and risk-factor study in Pernambuco. No host pathophysiological data.

species: Rangelia vitalii (pampas fox; not Babesia, not dog)
rationale: Single case in a pampas fox infected with Rangelia vitalii; a non-Canis canid and not a canine Babesia, with no dog data.
PCR prevalence and distribution survey in Japanese dogs with no host pathophysiological data.
Pathogen screening of ticks removed from dogs, with a zoonotic focus and no host data from infected dogs.

species: B. canis (reported as B. canis; method not stated in abstract)
rationale: Compares thyroid hormones, IL-6, urea and creatinine in 13 dogs with babesiosis against 10 controls and reports low T3 syndrome linked to IL-6 and azotaemia, which is endocrine and inflammatory pathophysiology.
PCR survey of Babesia in questing ticks in Poland; no dog host data.

Flow cytometric study of platelet activation and platelet-leukocyte aggregates in 36 B. rossi-infected dogs versus controls, with survival analysis. Already in the review as BG013 and screened as a new record.
Economic decision model of B. microti blood donor screening in humans; no dog data.
Tick distribution survey in the Baltic countries with no host pathophysiological data.
Case report of idiopathic IMHA in a dog that tested negative for Babesia; the dog is not Babesia-infected, so there are no eligible host data.
Molecular and serological survey in equids of the Pantanal; no dog data.

species: B. canis (58/60) and B. gibsoni (2/60), confirmed by PCR-RFLP and sequencing
rationale: Clinicopathological profile of 60 symptomatic dogs with CBC findings of thrombocytopenia and normocytic normochromic anaemia, so it counts as descriptive host evidence despite the molecular identification focus.
Corneal and conjunctival protozoal infections in dogs caused by other parasites; no Babesia.
Holographic microscopy of B. microti-parasitised mouse red cells; no dog data.

species: Red fox; B. vogeli not detected
rationale: Spatial survey of Anaplasma and Hepatozoon in red foxes; B. vogeli was not detected and there are no dog data.

species: B. canis (confirmed, PCR/IFAT; experimental tick transmission)
rationale: Based on the abstract: a fluralaner prevention trial whose endpoints are tick efficacy and infection prevention. Rectal temperature and clinical signs were monitored only to detect infection, and infected controls were rescue-treated with no host pathophysiological results reported. This matches earlier rounds, which excluded acaricide prevention trials.
rescue_reason: Borderline: the fluralaner trial infected control dogs with B. canis and, per the methods, monitored rectal temperature and clinical signs, but the abstract reports only tick efficacy and infection outcomes. Rescued for full-text check of host data in infected controls. Exclusion code treatment_efficacy may still hold.

rationale: Prevalence survey of vector-borne pathogens in rural Ugandan dogs and ticks with no host pathophysiological data.

species: B. bovis (enzyme); B. gibsoni (in vitro growth only)
rationale: Recombinant B. bovis aminopeptidase characterisation and in vitro growth inhibition by bestatin; no host data from infected dogs.
Bc28.1 gene polymorphism genotyping and its geographic distribution in blood samples from suspected cases; no host clinical or pathophysiological data.
Tick microRNA profiling with no dog or Babesia host data.
Seroprevalence and tick infestation survey in indigenous community dogs with no host pathophysiological data.
Parasite protein-export pathway in B. bovis and other apicomplexans; no dog or host data.
Molecular survey of tick-borne agents in cats; no dog data.

species: Leishmania infantum (B. canis serum used only as a cross-reactivity control)
rationale: Leishmania antigen for diagnosis and vaccination; B. canis sera serve only as cross-reactivity controls.
Black bears as tick hosts with B. microti detection in bears; no dog data.
Canine distemper outbreak report in which a few dogs had vector-borne infections including Babesia; no Babesia-specific host data can be separated out.
PCR and phylogeny of B. microti in questing ticks in Mongolia; no dog data.
Human case report of severe babesiosis treated with exchange transfusion; no dog data.

species: B. canis and B. vogeli, large vs small Babesia (literature review; status unspecified)

Seroprevalence survey of canine vector-borne diseases in Bulgaria with no host pathophysiological data.
Review of arthropod-borne diseases in human campers with no dog babesiosis content.

species: Babesia spp., focus on canine babesiosis (unspecified in abstract)
rationale: Review of babesiosis that centres on dogs and covers pathogenesis alongside taxonomy, epidemiology and control, so it is kept as a review of canine babesiosis. Its pathophysiology depth is only judged from the abstract.
Necropsy of two wild foxes infected with Rangelia vitalii; non-Canis canids and not a canine Babesia, with no dog data.
Two-case report of the first molecular identification of B. gibsoni in Slovakia; the abstract describes diagnosis and treatment with no distinct syndrome or mechanistic observation.
Measures serum canine pancreatic lipase in 87 B. rossi-infected dogs and relates it to SIRS and death, showing possible pancreatic involvement.

species: Toxoplasma gondii (B. gibsoni in vitro only as comparator)
rationale: In vitro effect of phytoecdysteroids on Toxoplasma in human and mouse cells; no dog host data.
Experimental B. gibsoni infection with longitudinal clinical, haematological, CRP and cytokine responses, showing the acute-phase and cytokine response.

species: B. vogeli, B. canis, Theileria annae (confirmed, PCR)

species: B. canis DNA in bat faeces
rationale: Screening of bat faeces for B. canis DNA; no dog host data.

species: Babesia sp. 'Spanish dog', B. gibsoni, B. vogeli (confirmed, PCR)

species: B. canis canis (naturally infected; confirmation method not stated)

species: B. canis canis (stated in title; method not available)

species: B. canis in Dermacentor reticulatus ticks (PCR)

Assay development and a survey of livestock on Caribbean islands, with no infected-dog host data.

species: B. gibsoni and B. vogeli (confirmed, qPCR)
