species: Human tick-borne infections, Babesia spp. in general
rationale: Review of emerging tick-borne infections in humans in China, with no canine host data.

species: B. vogeli DNA in ticks from cats
rationale: Pathogen DNA in ticks removed from cats, with no dog host data.
Seroprevalence survey and tick species identification in East China, with no host pathophysiological data.
Prevalence survey of parasitic and vector-borne pathogens in client-owned dogs in Albania, with no Babesia-specific host data in the abstract.
Molecular survey of tick-borne agents in dogs and ticks in the Pantanal, with no host pathophysiological data.
Rickettsia detection in ticks from dogs in Romania. Babesia is a screening add-on in ticks, with no dog host data.
Review of apheresis and exchange transfusion in human babesiosis, with no dog data.

species: B. canis, B. microti, B. venatorum in ticks (PCR)
rationale: Molecular detection of pathogens in ticks from dogs and vegetation in Serbia, with no host data.
In vitro drug study on Babesia bovis, with no dog data.
Literature review of the occurrence of vector-borne diseases in companion animals in Namibia, with no pathophysiological content.
Allele-specific PCR for the atovaquone-resistance cytochrome b variant in parasite DNA from infected dogs. It reports parasite genetics only, with no host data.
Development and evaluation of a recombinant BgP12 ELISA for serodiagnosis, with no host pathophysiology.

species: B. vogeli and T. annae in wild carnivores (PCR); no infected dogs
rationale: Molecular survey of vector-borne pathogens in wild and domestic carnivores and their ticks. None of the dogs were infected and no host pathophysiological data are reported.

From the abstract: a tick-transmission prevention trial whose endpoint is whether dogs acquire infection. Rectal temperature and clinical examination are used only to detect infection, and no host pathophysiological results are reported.
rescue_reason: Weak rescue. This is a prevention trial in which the B. canis challenge arm recorded rectal temperature and clinical examinations in infected dogs, so vector_tick understates it. The platelet counts belong to the E. canis arm only. The adjudicator should decide whether fever and clinical signs count as host markers.

rationale: Doctoral thesis on Bartonella infection in dogs and moose. It is not canine Babesia research.
Review of Ixodes tick-borne coinfection of B. burgdorferi and B. microti in ticks, reservoir hosts and humans, with no dog data.
Genetic polymorphism and selection analysis of four B. gibsoni antigen genes, with no host data.
Platelet indices in 96 B. rossi-infected dogs against 15 controls, with survivors and non-survivors compared. It reports activated platelets despite severe thrombocytopenia and the link to outcome.

species: B. canis and other canine Babesia spp. (review)
rationale: From the title and abstract: a narrative review of canine babesiosis with emphasis on B. canis. It covers immunological events and the clinical and pathological aspects of infection, which falls within the review's pathophysiology scope even though diagnostics are also covered.

species: Not applicable (Babesia only in PCR specificity tests)
rationale: Prevalence of zoonotic pathogens (Borrelia, Coxiella, Dirofilaria, Leptospira, Toxoplasma) in Taiwanese dogs. Babesia appears only as a cross-reactivity control.

From the abstract: a Hepatozoon haematology study in which Babesia is one of five coinfecting agents in 10 of 48 dogs. The coinfection comparison pools all agents, so no Babesia-specific host data can be separated out.
rescue_reason: Haematology of Hepatozoon-infected dogs reports anaemia and thrombocytopenia and compares coinfected dogs (20.8% with Babesia sp. among others) with non-coinfected dogs. The exclusion holds only if Babesia-coinfected dogs cannot be separated, which the adjudicator should check against the full text.

rationale: 18S rDNA characterisation of B. vogeli from dogs in Belém, with no host clinicopathological data.

species: B. vogeli (confirmed, PCR); mixed with E. canis and L. infantum
rationale: Serum nitric oxide, advanced oxidation protein products and antioxidant capacity in infected dogs against 17 controls. B. vogeli single-infection (n=5) and coinfection groups are reported separately, so Babesia-specific oxidative stress data can be separated out.

species: Rangelia vitalii (qPCR); Babesia only as specificity controls
rationale: qPCR assay for Rangelia vitalii, a different piroplasm. Babesia DNA is used only to test specificity.

From Crossref metadata (no abstract reachable; the Elsevier landing page did not load): a single-page item, J Comp Pathol 154(1):73, January 2016. That position matches the ESVP/ECVP annual meeting abstracts printed in that issue, so this is a conference abstract and not a full paper.

From the publisher landing page abstract: a microscopy and PCR prevalence survey of 130 stray dogs with age and sex associations and molecular characterisation. No haematological, clinical or biochemical data from infected dogs are reported.
Molecular detection of Babesia in ticks collected from asymptomatic dogs, with no host data.
Retrospective clinic prevalence and seasonality of parasitic diseases, with no host pathophysiological data.

species: B. gibsoni and B. canis (method not stated)
rationale: From the abstract, confirmed on the publisher landing page: a hospital prevalence study that ranks the causes of haemolytic anaemia. It reports no haematology or other host data broken down for Babesia-infected dogs.
rescue_reason: Haemolytic anaemia is an erythrocyte-injury syndrome, and the abstract attributes some cases to B. gibsoni and B. canis. Babesia-specific host data may therefore be extractable. The adjudicator should check the full text for haematology by cause. Rescued liberally.

species: B. canis (confirmed; natural and experimental infection)
rationale: Prognostic markers (lactate, triglycerides, phosphate, haematology, acute-phase response) in 7 survivors and 8 non-survivors, with follow-up in 3 experimentally infected dogs.
Serum cytokine concentrations in 97 B. rossi-infected dogs against 15 controls, linked to outcome. This is a record already in the review as BG014, screened as a new record on content.
Human case report from Ecuador, with no dog data.
Myocarditis in canine leishmaniasis. B. canis is mentioned only as a background cause of myocarditis, and there are no Babesia-infected dogs.
Human case report of severe B. microti infection, with no dog data.
Plant extract study in rats; 'gibsoni' is a plant species name, unrelated to Babesia.
Molecular survey of pathogens in field-collected ticks with no dog host data.
Clinical, haematological (PCV, leukogram) and outcome data in 103 dogs, Babesia-positive versus negative, so a clinicopathological profile of infected dogs.

species: Babesia sp. (unspecified, smear only; mixed haemoprotozoan infections)
rationale: Based on the abstract: a treatment study of mixed haemoprotozoan infections in dogs and cattle with haematology in all animals. Whether canine Babesia-specific haematology can be separated from other parasites and from cattle needs the full text.
PCR prevalence and risk-factor survey with no host pathophysiological data.

Based on the abstract: a routine single case of diagnosis, doxycycline treatment and transfusion for severe anaemia. The anaemia is the usual presentation, with no distinct syndrome or mechanistic observation.
rescue_reason: Single B. gibsoni case reports haematology in an infected dog (PCV 10%, Hb 2.6 g%) with recovery after transfusion, which the rescue rule covers even inside a treatment report. The full screen should decide whether the anaemia is a distinct syndrome or only a routine case.

species: B. canis and B. gibsoni (reported co-infection, method not stated)
rationale: Case report of acute renal failure as a babesiosis complication, a distinct organ-injury syndrome; the abstract is brief but the renal syndrome is the focus.

Based on the OpenAlex record: the only location is a Universidad de Guayaquil repository file named 'proyecto final', so this is a student degree project, not a peer-reviewed article. The title also shows an incidence survey.
rescue_reason: No abstract. The title is an incidence survey of B. canis in urban dogs, which does not rule out host haematology or other host markers, so it is rescued for full-text checking.

rationale: Ecology and distribution of ixodid ticks on dogs; no host data.

species: Babesia sp. (smear only; mixed with Ehrlichia and Anaplasma)
rationale: Based on the abstract: a routine single case of triple co-infection with diagnosis and treatment. Its cytopenias cannot be attributed to Babesia, so the mixed-infection rule is not met, and it describes no distinct syndrome.
rescue_reason: Case of Ehrlichia, Anaplasma and Babesia co-infection that reports thrombocytopenia, leukopenia and eosinopenia in an infected dog. Babesia-specific host data may not be separable from the co-infections, so the mixed-infection rule must be applied at full screen.

rationale: Duplicate record of PMID:27796110 (J S Afr Vet Assoc 87:e1-e3), which round 1 excluded as prevalence_epidemiology. Its PubMed abstract shows a distribution record confirmed by RLB, with no host data.
rescue_reason: No abstract. The short communication confirms B. vogeli in a dog in Namibia and the title does not rule out host data. It is probably a distribution record, so the full text should be checked.

rationale: Based on title and OpenAlex metadata only (Ann Parasitol vol 62, no pages; the landing page returned 403). This is probably a congress abstract that goes with PMID:26304014 (Vichova et al.). It may report clinicopathological data, but neither its format nor its content can be judged.
Post-mortem and histopathological comparison of five dogs dead from babesiosis with five from leptospirosis, describing septic shock, pulmonary oedema, haemolysis, DIC and hypoxic necrosis.

species: Babesia sp. (canine babesiosis, species not stated)
rationale: Bioinformatic analysis of the host serum proteome of dogs with babesiosis to predict regulatory miRNA markers; an omics study of the host response.

species: B. canis (confirmed, PCR/sequencing; Dirofilaria repens co-infection with a B. canis-only comparison group)
rationale: Probable duplicate record of PMID:27595920 (BMC Vet Res 2016, same authors and title). Its PubMed abstract compares anaemia, thrombocytopenia, ALP and urea between B. canis-only and co-infected dogs. If this Ann Parasitol record turns out to be only a congress abstract, it should be excluded as not_peer_reviewed in favour of the BMC paper.
rescue_reason: No abstract. The title covers dogs with concurrent babesiosis, which the title does not rule out as a source of host haematology. Babesia-specific host data would need to be separated from Dirofilaria.

rationale: Based on title and OpenAlex metadata only (PubVet 10(12):886-888; the CAB landing page is gone). This 3-page general review may or may not cover pathophysiology or clinical syndromes.

Based on title and OpenAlex metadata (J Vet Parasitol 30(2):86-89; no abstract reachable). The title and the short format show a molecular detection and prevalence study, with no sign of host pathophysiological data.
rescue_reason: No abstract. The title describes naturally infected dogs with B. canis, so host haematology or biochemistry cannot be ruled out from the title. The full text should be checked.

rationale: Based on title and OpenAlex metadata only (ICAR repository PDF was unreachable). The title reports two organ complications, B. gibsoni-induced hepatopathy and acute renal injury, which count as a distinct complication syndrome under the case-report rule. Confirm the clinicopathological detail at extraction.
Molecular characterisation of B. canis in ticks; no host data.

species: B. bovis and B. bigemina (cattle, buffalo)
rationale: Bovine and buffalo infection survey; no dog data.

species: B. vogeli (confirmed, qPCR; all co-infected with L. infantum)
rationale: Based on the abstract: qPCR detection of pathogen DNA in pooled brain tissue of Leishmania-infected dogs. It reports no host pathology, and Babesia cannot be separated from Leishmania or Ehrlichia.
rescue_reason: qPCR detects B. vogeli DNA in the brain tissue of three co-infected dogs, a possible cerebral tissue-distribution observation. No host pathology is reported and Babesia must be separated from Leishmania, so the full text should be checked against the exclusion.

rationale: Case report of a distinct neurological presentation (paraplegia) in B. gibsoni infection, with haemato-biochemical changes including hypoglycaemia and raised creatinine.
Case of Rangelia vitalii infection; Babesia canis and B. gibsoni PCR were negative.

species: Leishmania infantum (Babesia canis sera used only as cross-reactivity controls)
rationale: Leishmania serodiagnosis antigen study; Babesia sera were only negative controls.
Detection of B. vogeli in Rhipicephalus sanguineus ticks; no host data.
ITS1 sequence conservation among isolates; parasite genetics with no host data.

species: B. canis canis (confirmed, PCR and 18S sequencing)
rationale: Fatal rapidly progressive babesiosis in a splenectomised dog with severe thrombocytopenia and high parasitaemia, a mechanistic observation on the spleen's protective role.

Based on the abstract: a treatment trial in 8 naturally infected dogs with parasite-clearance endpoints. It states that all dogs had mild to severe anaemia and thrombocytopenia, so the full text needs checking for tabulated haematology, which would make it eligible.
rescue_reason: Treatment comparison in naturally infected B. gibsoni dogs. The abstract reports mild-to-severe anaemia and thrombocytopenia in all dogs, which is host haematology in infected dogs, so the treatment-trial exclusion should be re-checked at full screen.

species: B. gibsoni (confirmed, PCR; CYTb M121I mutation)
rationale: Real-time PCR assay to detect a drug-resistance mutation; no host data.
Prevalence of B. annae DNA in red fox lung exudate; no dog data.
Based on PubMed metadata: a Vet Record letter/comment (178(7):172) with no abstract. Its MeSH terms are dog transportation and commerce, so it reports no research data.
rescue_reason: Letter or comment with no abstract. The MeSH terms point to dog transport, so data are probably absent, but the generic title does not rule out host data. The adjudicator should check the full text; not_research probably stands.

rationale: Epizootological survey of infection rate and seasonality with no host pathophysiological data.
Experimental B. microti infection in macaques; no dog data.
Acaricide speed-of-kill trial on tick infestations; no Babesia infection or host data.
Human case report of persistent babesiosis on rituximab.
Plasma proteomics at admission in dogs with uncomplicated babesiosis, SIRS or MODS versus healthy dogs, identifying differentially expressed proteins (complement inhibitors, paraoxonase 1, apoA-I).
Cryopreservation media for in vitro parasite culture; no host data.
Seasonal distribution of B. canis genotypes in questing ticks; no dog data.

Duplicate record of https://openalex.org/W2370925246, the English title of the same atovaquone/proguanil plus azithromycin trial, so it gets the same decision. The full text needs checking for haematology data in the infected dogs.
rescue_reason: Duplicate record of https://openalex.org/W2370925246: the English title of the same atovaquone/proguanil trial in naturally infected B. gibsoni dogs, with the same rescue decision.

rationale: Duplicate record of https://openalex.org/W2511694410: PCR prevalence and risk-factor survey with no host pathophysiological data.

species: Babesia spp. in ticks (no dog data)
rationale: Prevalence and phylogeny of Babesia in Ixodes ticks in Latvia. No host data from infected dogs.
County-scale distribution of Ixodes ticks in the US. No canine Babesia host data.

species: Not specified (babesiosis named only in a list)
rationale: Based on the abstract: a general narrative review of point-of-care lactate in small animals. Babesiosis is named once among conditions with raised lactate, so canine babesiosis pathophysiology is not the subject and the review adds no babesia-specific content.
rescue_reason: Narrative review of point-of-care lactate. The abstract states that blood lactate is significantly raised in canine babesiosis, which is a host biochemical marker. The content is general and the mention is brief, so this is low-yield, but the adjudicator should check it. The first screener's topic reason is otherwise right.

rationale: Practice article on B. canis distribution, tick identification and control in the UK. No host pathophysiological content.
Molecular survey of pathogens in ticks from China. No dog host data.
PCR survey of piroplasms and Hepatozoon in ticks from Palestine. No host pathophysiological data.

Prevalence study in dogfighting dogs that also reports PCV and anaemia in infected dogs, with anaemia associated with B. gibsoni infection (OR 2.5). It meets the rule that a survey with host haematology is included.

Based on the title and PubMed metadata (2-page Vet Rec letter from APHA/PHE, no abstract): a report of B. canis detection in dogs and Dermacentor ticks in Essex. The focus is occurrence and the vector, not host pathophysiology.
rescue_reason: Letter with no abstract. The title reports B. canis detected in dogs and associated ticks, so host clinical or haematological data cannot be ruled out. Adjudicator should check the full letter.

rationale: Experimental B. bigemina infection in cattle. No dog data.
Veterinary Record letter with no abstract, on B. canis in ticks in Essex.
Molecular detection and TRAP-gene diversity of B. gibsoni in Indian dogs. No host pathophysiological data.
News item on tick treatment requirements for travelling dogs.
Letter/comment on imported disease threat to UK dogs, with no abstract or data.

Based on the abstract: an occurrence survey of vector-borne pathogens. The anaemia, thrombocytopenia and jaundice are reported only for Rangelia vitalii-positive dogs, and there are no host findings for the B. vogeli-infected dogs.
rescue_reason: Survey of vector-borne pathogens in dogs and cats in Brazil. The abstract reports anaemia, thrombocytopenia, jaundice and bleeding in dogs, but these are attributed to Rangelia vitalii, not Babesia. B. vogeli dogs have no reported host findings, so Babesia-specific data cannot be separated. Likely excluded at adjudication, but flagged because the haematology is in piroplasm-infected dogs.

rationale: Based on the title and OpenAlex record (Kuleš, Gotić, Mrljak, Barić Rafaj; CroRIS repository, no DOI, venue or abstract): the topic, anticoagulant pathways in B. canis babesiosis, is eligible. The CroRIS page has a bot check, so the publication type could not be seen; it may be a conference abstract. Full-text check needed.
Letter/comment on canine infections imported to the UK, with no abstract or data.
Dermacentor reticulatus foci and seroprevalence of B. canis in Italian dogs. No host pathophysiological data.
Peroxiredoxin from B. bovis parasite. No dog data.
Prevalence survey of vector-borne pathogens in Haitian dogs. No host pathophysiological data.
Editorial on autochthonous canine babesiosis in the UK.

Based on PubMed, Europe PMC and Crossref metadata (Wiley page 403; the repository PDF is a different paper): a single-page JSAP case item with no abstract and MeSH major topic 'diagnosis'. It reads as a routine autochthonous diagnosis with no sign of a distinct syndrome or mechanism.
JAMA review of human Lyme disease, anaplasmosis and babesiosis. No dog data.
B. microti infection in human patients in Poland.
Cloning and heat-shock response of the parasite HSP90 gene. No host data.
Molecular prevalence survey in Thai stray dogs. No host pathophysiological data.
Title concerns the availability of treatments for canine babesiosis, and no abstract is given. The topic is treatment access (likely a letter), not host pathophysiology.
Identification of two recombinant B. canis antigens for serodiagnostic ELISA and ICT. No host pathophysiological data.
Molecular survey of tick-borne pathogens in asymptomatic dogs in Cape Verde. No Babesia was found and no host data are reported.

species: T. equi / B. caballi in horses and donkeys
rationale: Equine piroplasmosis in horses and donkeys. No dog data.
Seroprevalence survey of military dogs in Portugal. No host pathophysiological data.

Based on the abstract: a case series of Borrelia persica relapsing fever. The anaemia and thrombocytopenia are attributed to Borrelia, and the Babesia co-infected dogs cannot be separated out, so it fails the mixed-infection rule.
rescue_reason: Case series of B. persica (Borrelia) in five dogs and five cats. The abstract reports anaemia and thrombocytopenia in dogs, and three dogs were co-infected with Babesia. The findings cannot be attributed to Babesia, so the adjudicator should decide, but the haematology is in dogs with a Babesia co-infection.

rationale: Vector-borne pathogens in cats and their fleas and ticks. No dog data.

species: B. vogeli, B. gibsoni, Babesia sp. (confirmed, PCR)
rationale: Molecular prevalence survey in dogs from Luanda. No host pathophysiological data.
Prevalence survey of vector-borne pathogens in Cambodian dogs. No host data.
Erratum, with no content. The original paper concerns red foxes.

species: B. canis (1 dog, PCR); T. annae in foxes
rationale: Prevalence survey of vector-borne pathogens in dogs and foxes in Brandenburg. No host pathophysiological data.
Acaricide efficacy against Rhipicephalus sanguineus on dogs. No Babesia infection or host data.

species: Babesia spp. in ticks and rodents
rationale: Babesia in ticks and wildlife in Slovakia. No dog host data.

species: B. canis canis (confirmed, PCR and 18S sequencing)
rationale: Based on the abstract: a case report of probable in utero transmission. The bitch was infected in week 7 of pregnancy and her three puppies developed clinical disease at 8-9 weeks, with identical sequences. Congenital infection is a distinct presentation and a mechanistic observation, so it is more than a routine case.
rescue_reason: Case report of probable in utero transmission of B. canis canis from a bitch to her puppies, with clinical disease in the puppies and PCR confirmation. The vertical or congenital transmission route is a mechanistic observation and a distinct presentation, so the first screener's routine-case reason does not hold.

rationale: Fluralaner prevention of tick transmission of B. canis, with infection status as the endpoint. No host pathophysiological outcomes.
Molecular detection of piroplasms in biting flies; no dog host data.
Review of Dermacentor reticulatus ecology and distribution; no host pathophysiology.
Oxidative stress and haematology in Babesia-infected calves; no dog data.

Based on the abstract: a single B. gibsoni case with routine findings (anaemia, thrombocytopenia, fever, splenomegaly) and a report of response to a drug combination. It describes no distinct syndrome or mechanistic observation, so the routine case report rule applies.
rescue_reason: Single B. gibsoni-infected dog with haematology before and after treatment (Hb 7.7 g/dl, platelets 86,000/µl, fever, splenomegaly). Host haematological markers are present, so the routine-case reason is arguable. Adjudicator to judge whether it describes a distinct syndrome.

rationale: Drug efficacy study in immunodeficient mice; no dog data.

species: B. canis, B. vogeli, B. gibsoni, B. vulpes (review)
rationale: Based on the abstract: a narrative review of canine babesiosis in Europe that compares clinical signs and prognosis for each species. The paper (Solano-Gallego et al. 2016) also covers laboratory abnormalities and complications for each species, so it fits the review criterion on clinical syndromes and complications.
Parasite genomics of B. microti from human infections; no dog data.

Based on the abstract: the 5 Babesia-positive dogs were seropositive but PCR-negative, so they show exposure, not active infection. The haemogram and clinical data are reported for the whole group of 58 suspect dogs and are not split by Babesia status, so the mixed-infection rule is not met.
rescue_reason: Haemogram and clinical signs (haemorrhagic diathesis, fever) reported for 58 suspected dogs, including 5 Babesia-seropositive dogs. Haematology is not split by Babesia status, so the mixed-infection rule needs adjudicator checking.

species: B. microti, B. venatorum in ticks
rationale: Pathogen detection in ticks collected from pets; no host pathophysiology.

Title only: there is no abstract in OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar, Crossref or Europe PMC, and the Springer page is behind a sign-in redirect. The title points to thyroid and oxidative-stress data in dogs with babesiosis, probably as a group separate from ehrlichiosis, but the full text must confirm that the Babesia data can be separated.

Based on the one-page English abstract in the publisher PDF: a treatment study of transfusing cryopreserved packed red cells after Piro-Stop. The only endpoints are percentage rises in Hb, Hct and RBC count against untransfused dogs, with no mechanistic or pathophysiological outcomes.

Duplicate record of DOI:10.15407/cryo26.02.186 (Russian-language title, same journal page 186). It is a treatment study of red-cell transfusion with only Hb, Hct and RBC response endpoints, so the decision is the same.
Seroprevalence survey of clinically healthy dogs; no host pathophysiology.
Canine parvovirus epidemiology in which Babesia appears only as a rare co-infection; no Babesia host data.

Based on the abstract: the subject is Anaplasma platys infection. B. vogeli occurs only as a co-infection in 3 dogs, and the findings are grouped as mono- versus co-infected dogs. No Babesia-specific host data can be separated, so the mixed-infection rule is not met.
rescue_reason: Haematology and clinical findings in 32 dogs with Anaplasma platys, including 2 B. vogeli co-infected dogs and 1 triple infection. Babesia-specific data are not separated, so the mixed-infection rule must be checked by the adjudicator rather than applied here.

rationale: Molecular prevalence and genotyping of piroplasms in Tunisian dogs; no host pathophysiological data.

species: B. microti (human, PCR); dog not tested
rationale: Based on the HKMJ landing page: the case is human B. microti babesiosis in a dog owner. The article does not report whether the pet dog was tested for Babesia and gives no clinical or laboratory data on the dog.
rescue_reason: Abstract missing. The title says the babesiosis was acquired from a pet dog, so the source dog's infection or clinical data may be reported, and the title does not rule this out. Adjudicator to read the full text.

rationale: Surveillance of Babesia cases and tick activity from electronic health records; no host pathophysiology.

species: B. gibsoni (co-infection with Leptospira and D. repens)
rationale: Title only: no abstract could be found, and the Springer page is behind a sign-in redirect. The title describes clinical management of a single dog with a triple infection including leptospirosis. Findings in such a case cannot be attributed to Babesia, and the title points to a routine management report rather than a distinct syndrome.
Tick-borne pathogens in camels; no dog data.

species: B. gibsoni, B. canis vogeli (confirmed, PCR)
rationale: Molecular identification and prevalence of Babesia in dogs in Kerala; no host pathophysiological data.
Recombinant parasite peroxiredoxin from B. microti; parasite biology with no dog data.

species: B. canis (ticks, PCR); dogs smear-confirmed in 19 of 33
rationale: Based on the abstract: the study is about Babesia occurrence in ticks. Its clinical signs (with anaemia noted only clinically, in 4 dogs) are counted across all 33 suspect dogs, not the 19 smear-confirmed dogs, and there are no haematology or biochemistry data. This is not a usable clinicopathological profile of infected dogs.
rescue_reason: Clinical signs in 33 suspected dogs, with anaemia in 4, haematuria in 8 and tremor in 6, and babesiosis confirmed microscopically in 19. Anaemia and organ-related signs are host data, so the no-haematology reason looks wrong.

species: B. canis (severe forms; method not stated)
rationale: MRI shows CNS lesions in all dogs with severe B. canis infection, so it provides host evidence of cerebral involvement. It also tests a contrast agent, but that does not remove the host data.

species: B. canis (confirmed, PCR) with Dirofilaria repens co-infection
rationale: Compares haematology and biochemistry between B. canis dogs with and without D. repens co-infection, with anaemia, thrombocytopenia, ALP and urea. It reports severity data for infected dogs and Babesia-only dogs can be separated.
Review of the diagnostic protocol and of therapy by species, with no host pathophysiology.
Equine piroplasmosis prevalence; no dog data.

Guidelines paper that also reports haematology and biochemistry by disease severity in infected dogs: erythropenia, thrombocytopenia, bilirubin, urea, creatinine and glucose. It also includes parasitaemia by age and an antioxidant treatment, so it qualifies as a clinicopathological profile.
Pathogen surveillance in African lions; no dog data.

species: Babesia spp. (co-infection with H. canis, 1 dog, smear)
rationale: Based on the abstract: a haematology study of H. canis infection. The one Babesia-positive dog was also infected with H. canis, and the authors state its changes cannot be attributed to a single agent, so no Babesia-specific host data can be separated.
rescue_reason: Haematology of H. canis-infected dogs, including one dog co-infected with Babesia spp. and reporting anaemia. Individual-level separation may be possible, so the adjudicator should check against the mixed-infection rule.

rationale: Practical overview of several tick-borne diseases for veterinary nurses. It is not a pathophysiology review of canine babesiosis.

Retrospective study of 92 dogs with large-form babesiosis, showing reticulocyte profile and fluorescence ratio changes. Parasitised red cells distort the automated reticulocyte count. The analytic artefact is borderline, but it does report erythrocyte data in infected dogs.
Editorial on canine babesiosis emergence in the UK; no abstract and no data.
Review of the epidemiology of piroplasmids in wild carnivores and tick vectors; no host pathophysiology.
Haematological profile of 101 dogs with parasitologically confirmed Babesia, with anaemia in 50.5% and thrombocytopenia in 84.2%. This is a clinicopathological profile, so it is included.
B. microti genomics and expression profiling with immune screening; no dog data.

Case report with a mechanistic observation: parasitised red cells are counted as reticulocytes by the analyser, with nonregenerative anaemia and pancytopenia. This is distinct from a routine diagnosis and treatment case.
